<h2 id="introduction">Introduction</h2>
<p>The 4D Labs family of embedded graphics processors are powered by a highly optimised soft-core virtual engine, E.V.E. (Extensible Virtual Engine). EVE was designed and created by 4D Labs in the early 2000’s and should not be confused by FTDI’s solution of EVE, which was developed a decent decade or so later.</p>
<p>EVE is a proprietary, high performance virtual processor with an extensive byte-code instruction set optimised to execute compiled 4DGL programs. 4DGL (4D Graphics Language) was specifically developed from ground up for the EVE engine core. It is a high-level language which is easy to learn and simple to understand yet powerful enough to tackle many embedded graphics applications.</p>
<p>4DGL is a graphics-oriented language allowing rapid application development. An extensive library of graphics, text and file system functions and the ease of use of a language that combines the best elements and syntax structure of languages such as C, Basic, Pascal, etc. Programmers familiar with these languages will feel right at home with 4DGL. It includes many familiar instructions such as <code>IF..ELSE..ENDIF, WHILE..WEND, REPEAT..UNTIL, GOSUB..ENDSUB, GOTO</code> as well as a wealth of (chip-resident) internal functions that include <code>SERIN, SEROUT, GFX_LINE, GFX_CIRCLE</code> and many more.</p>
<p>This document covers the internal (chip-resident) functions available for the PIXXI-28 and PIXXI-44 processors. This document should be used in conjunction with the <a href="../">4DGL Programmers Reference Manual</a>.</p>

<h2 class="page-break" id="c-type-functions">C Type Functions</h2>
<h3 id="isdigit">isdigit</h3>
<p>Tests the character parameter and returns a 1 if the character is an ASCII digit else returns a 0.
Valid Range: "0123456789"</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>isdigit(char);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the ASCII character for the test</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: 1 if character is ASCII digit, otherwise 0</p>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="isxdigit">isxdigit</h3>
<p>Tests the character parameter and returns a 1 if the character is an ascii hexadecimal digit else returns a 0.
Valid Range: "0123456789ABCDEF"</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>isxdigit(char);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the ASCII character for the test</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: 1 if character is ASCII hexadecimal digit, otherwise 0</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: Refer to <a href="#isdigit">isdigit()</a> for an example</p>
<h3 class="page-break" id="isupper">isupper</h3>
<p>Tests the character parameter and returns a 1 if the character is an ASCII uppercase letter else returns a 0.
Valid Range: "ABCDEF....WXYZ"</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>isupper(char);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>

<h2 class="page-break" id="crc-functions">CRC Functions</h2>
<h3 id="crc_csum_8">crc_CSUM_8</h3>
<p>Calculates the Checksum CRC as an 8 bit number.
This is equivalent to simple addition of all bytes and returning the negated sum an 8 bit value.
For the standard test string "123456789", crc_CSUM_8 will return 0x23.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>crc_CSUM_8(buf, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Source memory buffer. This is a string pointer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of bytes to be used to generate the CRC.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: The generated 8-bit checksum CRC</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-5-1" name="__codelineno-5-1" href="#__codelineno-5-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">crc</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-5-2" name="__codelineno-5-2" href="#__codelineno-5-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">buf</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">];</span>
<a id="__codelineno-5-3" name="__codelineno-5-3" href="#__codelineno-5-3"></a><span class="c1">// [0x31, 0x32, 0x33, 0x34, 0x35, 0x36, 0x37, 0x38, 0x39]</span>
<a id="__codelineno-5-4" name="__codelineno-5-4" href="#__codelineno-5-4"></a><span class="n">to</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">buf</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"123456789"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-5-5" name="__codelineno-5-5" href="#__codelineno-5-5"></a><span class="nl">crc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">crc_CSUM_8</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">str_Ptr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">buf</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<!-- TODO: Check if count should be 9 instead of 10 -->

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>If you calculate all of the incoming data <strong>including</strong> the CRC, the result should be 0x00.</p>

<h3 id="disp_setgram">disp_setGRAM</h3>
<p>Prepares the (Graphics RAM) GRAM area for user access. The lower 16 bits of the pixel count in the selected area is returned This is usually all that is needed unless GRAM area exceeds 256<sup>2</sup>. A copy of the 32-bit value can be found in GRAM_PIXEL_COUNT_LO and GRAM_PIXEL_COUNT_HI.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>disp_setGRAM(x1, y1, x2, y2);</code></p>

</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Left position in the GRAM window</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bottom position in the GRAM window</td>
</tr>
<tr>

</tr>

<h3 class="page-break" id="disp_wrgram">disp_WrGRAM</h3>

<h3 class="page-break" id="disp_sync">disp_Sync</h3>
<p>Allows the program to synchronise writing to the hardware for flicker free operation.
Some experimentation may be needed to find an optimum line for disp_Sync depending on the graphics operation.
The higher the value, the slower the throughput.
A certain point will be reached (number of scanlines + blanking lines within the vertical retrace period)
where it will just 'hang up' stopping the entire process.
Eg, in 640x480 mode, if the 'lines' value is 507, operation will be slowest
(as it’s right at the end of the blanking period)
and 508 will cause a hangup situation as it is above the highest scanline value. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>disp_Sync(line);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">line</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">scan line</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: 16-bit value in the register</p>
<!-- TODO: Add example -->

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Applies to 4.3” modules only. </p>
</div>
<h3 id="disp_disconnect">disp_Disconnect</h3>
<p>This function disconnects the display driver pins and/or reconfigures it to achieve its lowest possible power consumption. Use after disabling peripheral power to ensure the minimal power usage by the display. <a href="#disp_init">disp_Init()</a> should be used to reinitialise the display.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>disp_Disconnect();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<!-- TODO: Add example -->

<h3 id="disp_init">disp_Init</h3>
<p>This function is used to initialise the display. </p>
<p>This is useful in several situations, however mainly for modules which can disable the power supply to the display for low power sleep modes. This function is required to re-initialise the display once power to the display has been restored, so the display is usable once again. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>disp_Init();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<!-- TODO: Add example -->

<h3 id="file_findfirst">file_FindFirst</h3>
<p>Returns true if at least one file exists that satisfies the file argument.
Wildcards are usually used so if file_FindFirst returns true, further tests can be made using

Note that the stream behaviour is the same as <a href="#file_dir">file_Dir()</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_FindFirst(fname);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<!-- TODO: Confirm if 'fname' accepts a string (byte-aligned) pointer or array (word-aligned) pointer -->

<h3 id="file_findnext">file_FindNext</h3>
<p>Returns true if more file exists that satisfies the file argument that was given for <a href="#file_findfirst">file_FindFirst</a>.
Wildcards must be used for <a href="#file_findfirst">file_FindFirst()</a>, else this function will always return zero
as the only occurence will have already been found. Note that the stream behaviour is the same as <a href="#file_dir">file_Dir()</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_FindNext();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: 1 if at least one file exists that satisfies the criteria in <a href="#file_findfirst">file_FindFirst()</a>, 0 otherwise</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_open">file_Open</h3>
<p>Returns handle if file exists. The file "handle" created is now used as reference for "filename" for further file functions such as <a href="#file_close">file_Close()</a>, etc. For <code>FILE_WRITE</code> and <code>FILE_APPEND</code> modes (<code>'w'</code> and <code>'a'</code>) the file is created if it does not exist. </p>
<p>If the file is opened for append and it already exists, the file pointer is set to the end of the file ready for appending, else the file pointer will be set to the start of the newly created file.</p>
<p>If the file was opened successfully, the internal error number is set to 0 (ie: - no errors) and can be read with the <a href="#file_error">file_Error()</a> function.</p>
<p>For <code>FILE_READ</code> mode (<code>'r'</code>) the file must exist else a null handle (0) is returned and the 'file not found' error number is set which can be read with the <a href="#file_error">file_Error()</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_Open(fname, mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filename of the file to be opened (passed as a string)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><code>FILE_READ</code> (<code>'r'</code>), <code>FILE_WRITE</code> (<code>'w'</code>) or <code>FILE_APPEND</code> (<code>'a'</code>)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<!-- TODO: Confirm if 'fname' accepts a string (byte-aligned) pointer or array (word-aligned) pointer -->

<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: File handle if file exists, null (0) otherwise.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-17-1" name="__codelineno-17-1" href="#__codelineno-17-1"></a><span class="nl">handle</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Open</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"myfile.txt"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sc">'r'</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>This function is only available for use on the uSD based PmmC version.</li>
<li>If a file is opened for write mode <code>'w'</code>, and the file already exists, the operation will fail. Unlike C and some other languages where the file will be erased ready for re-writing when opened for writing, 4DGL offers a simple level of protection that ensures that a file must be purposely erased before being re-written.</li>
<li>A file opened with FILE_APPEND may be randomly read and or written. Also any altered file will have the Archive bit set in the directory entry.</li>
</ul>
</div>

<h3 id="file_seek">file_Seek</h3>
<p>Places the file pointer at the required position in a file that has been opened in <code>'r'</code> (read) or <code>'a'</code> (append) mode. In append mode, file_Seek does not expand a filesize, instead, the file pointer (handle) is set to the end position of the file, eg:- assuming the file size is 10000 bytes, file_Seek(handle, 0, 0x1234); will set the file position to 0x00001234 (byte position 4660) for the file handle, so subsequent data may be read from that position onwards with <a href="#file_getc">file_GetC(...)</a>, <a href="#file_getw">file_GetW(...)</a>, <a href="#file_gets">file_GetS(...)</a>, or an image can be displayed with <a href="#file_image">file_Image(...)</a>. Conversely, <a href="#file_putc">file_PutC(...)</a>, <a href="#file_putw">file_PutW(...)</a> and <a href="#file_puts">file_PutS(...)</a> can write to the file at the position. A <code>FE_EOF</code> (end of file error) will occur if you try to write or read past the end of the file. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_Seek(handle, HiWord, LoWord);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">File handle created by <a href="#file_open">file_Open</a> referencing the file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">HiWord</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the upper 16bits of the memory pointer into the file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LoWord</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the lower 16bits of the memory pointer into the file</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: True if successful (usually ignored)</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-20-1" name="__codelineno-20-1" href="#__codelineno-20-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Seek</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hSource</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x0000</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x1234</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This function is only available for use on the uSD based PmmC version.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="file_index">file_Index</h3>
<p>Places the file pointer at the position in a file that has been opened in <code>'r'</code> (read) or <code>'a'</code> (append) mode. In append mode, file_Index does not expand a filesize, instead, the file pointer (handle) is set to the end position of the file, eg:- assuming the record size is 100 bytes, file_Index(handle, 0, 100, 22); will set the file position to 2200 for the file handle, so subsequent data may be read from that position onwards with <a href="#file_getc">file_GetC(...)</a>, <a href="#file_getw">file_GetW(...)</a>, <a href="#file_gets">file_GetS(...)</a>, or an image can be displayed with <a href="#file_image">file_Image(...)</a>. Conversely, <a href="#file_putc">file_PutC(...)</a>, <a href="#file_putw">file_PutW(...)</a> and <a href="#file_puts">file_PutS(...)</a> can write to the file at the position. A <code>FE_EOF</code> (end of file error) will occur if you try to write or read past the end of the file.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_Index(handle, HiSize, LoSize, recordNum);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">File handle created by <a href="#file_open">file_Open</a> referencing the file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">HiSize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the upper 16bits of the size of the file records</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LoSize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the lower 16bits of the size of the file records</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">recordNum</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The index of the required record</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: True if successful (usually ignored)</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-21-1" name="__codelineno-21-1" href="#__codelineno-21-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Index</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hSource</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">22</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This function is only available for use on the uSD based PmmC version.</p>
</div>

<h3 id="file_screencapture">file_ScreenCapture</h3>
<p>Save an image of the screen shot to file at the current file position.</p>
<p>The image can later be displayed with <a href="#file_image">file_Image(...)</a>. The file may be opened in append mode to accumulate multiple images. Later, the images can be displayed with <a href="#file_seek">file_Seek(...)</a>. The image is saved from x, y (with respect to top left corner), and the capture area is determined by "width" and "height".</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_ScreenCapture(x, y, width, height, handle);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">X-position of the image to be captured</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Y-position of the image to be captured</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">width</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Width of the area to be captured</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">height</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Height of the area to be captured</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">File handle created by <a href="#file_open">file_Open</a> referencing the file for storing the image(s)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: 0 if successful</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-26-1" name="__codelineno-26-1" href="#__codelineno-26-1"></a><span class="n">file_Mount</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span>
<a id="__codelineno-26-2" name="__codelineno-26-2" href="#__codelineno-26-2"></a><span class="nl">hFile</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Open</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"test.img"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sc">'a'</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// open a file to save the image </span>
<a id="__codelineno-26-3" name="__codelineno-26-3" href="#__codelineno-26-3"></a><span class="n">file_ScreenCapture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hFile</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="c1">// save an area </span>
<a id="__codelineno-26-4" name="__codelineno-26-4" href="#__codelineno-26-4"></a><span class="n">file_ScreenCapture</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hFile</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// (save another area) </span>
<a id="__codelineno-26-5" name="__codelineno-26-5" href="#__codelineno-26-5"></a><span class="n">file_Close</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hFile</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                       </span><span class="c1">// now close the file </span>
<a id="__codelineno-26-6" name="__codelineno-26-6" href="#__codelineno-26-6"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-26-7" name="__codelineno-26-7" href="#__codelineno-26-7"></a><span class="c1">// and to display the saved area(s)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-26-8" name="__codelineno-26-8" href="#__codelineno-26-8"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-26-9" name="__codelineno-26-9" href="#__codelineno-26-9"></a><span class="nl">hFile</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Open</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"test.img"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sc">'r'</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// open the saved file </span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_putc">file_PutC</h3>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_gets">file_GetS</h3>
<p>This function reads a line of text to a buffer (specified by "*string") from a file at the current file position indicated by the associated file-position pointer and advances the pointer appropriately. Characters are read until either a newline or an EOF is received or until the specified maximum "size" is reached. In all cases, the string is null terminated. The file must be previously opened with <code>'r'</code> (read) mode. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_GetS(*string, size, handle);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>

<td style="text-align: left;">Destination buffer to store the string in</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The maximum number of bytes to be read from the file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">File handle created by <a href="#file_open">file_Open</a> referencing the file to read from</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Number of characters read from file (excluding the null teminator) </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-32-1" name="__codelineno-32-1" href="#__codelineno-32-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_GetS</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mystring</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">80</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_loadfunction">file_LoadFunction</h3>
<p>Load a function or program from disk and return a function pointer to the allocation.
The function can then be invoked just like any other function would be called via a function pointer. Parameters may be passed to it in a conventional way. The function may be discarded at any time when no longer required, thus freeing its memory resources.</p>
<p>The loaded function can be discarded with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(..)</a>. Note that any pointer references passed to the child function may not include references to the parents DATA statements or any static string references. Any string or array information must be in the parent’s global or local memory space. The reason for this is that DATA statements and static strincs are contained in the parents CODE segment and cannot be accessed by the child process.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_LoadFunction(fname);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filename of the 4DGL application program that is about to be loaded into RAM</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<!-- TODO: Confirm if 'fname' accepts a string (byte-aligned) pointer or array (word-aligned) pointer -->

<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Pointer to the memory allocation where the function has been loaded from file which can be then used as a function call</p>

<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This function is only available for use on the uSD based PmmC version.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_run">file_Run</h3>
<p>Any memory allocations in the main FLASH program are released, however, the stack and globals are maintained. </p>
<p>The function 'main' in the called program accepts the arguments, if any. If arglistptr is 0, no arguments are passed, else arglistptr points to an array, the first element containing the number of additional elements in the array which contain the arguments.</p>
<p>The disk does not need to be mounted, file_Run automatically mounts the drive.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_Run(fname, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filename of the 4DGL child program to be loaded into RAM and executed</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<!-- TODO: Confirm if 'fname' accepts a string (byte-aligned) pointer or array (word-aligned) pointer -->

<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Value returned by main function in the called program</p>

<a id="__codelineno-37-45" name="__codelineno-37-45" href="#__codelineno-37-45"></a><span class="cm">/*===================================================================</span>
<a id="__codelineno-37-46" name="__codelineno-37-46" href="#__codelineno-37-46"></a><span class="cm">Redraw the button matrix. Only draw buttons that have changed state.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-37-47" name="__codelineno-37-47" href="#__codelineno-37-47"></a><span class="cm">The top lef corner of the button matrix is set with the xorg and yorg parameters depending on the font and text string width, the button matrix dynamically resizes.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-37-48" name="__codelineno-37-48" href="#__codelineno-37-48"></a><span class="cm">Parameters:-</span>
<a id="__codelineno-37-49" name="__codelineno-37-49" href="#__codelineno-37-49"></a><span class="cm">maxwidth    = rhs from xorg (in pixels) to cause wrap at rhs</span>
<a id="__codelineno-37-50" name="__codelineno-37-50" href="#__codelineno-37-50"></a><span class="cm">maxwidth    = maximum matrix width (in pixel units)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-37-51" name="__codelineno-37-51" href="#__codelineno-37-51"></a><span class="cm">buttoncount = number of buttons to display</span>
<a id="__codelineno-37-52" name="__codelineno-37-52" href="#__codelineno-37-52"></a><span class="cm">font        = FONT1 to FONT4</span>
<a id="__codelineno-37-53" name="__codelineno-37-53" href="#__codelineno-37-53"></a><span class="cm">xorg:yorg   = top left corner of button array</span>
<a id="__codelineno-37-54" name="__codelineno-37-54" href="#__codelineno-37-54"></a><span class="cm">NB:- The  touch detect matrix array is updated when any button changes state.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-37-55" name="__codelineno-37-55" href="#__codelineno-37-55"></a><span class="cm">When you need to draw the matrix for the first instance of the matrix, you must</span>
<a id="__codelineno-37-56" name="__codelineno-37-56" href="#__codelineno-37-56"></a><span class="cm">call with mode = 1 to instantiate the buttons.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-37-57" name="__codelineno-37-57" href="#__codelineno-37-57"></a><span class="cm">call with mode = 0 for normal button action.</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_runspeed">file_RunSpeed</h3>
<p>This is similar to <a href="#file_run">file_Run</a> with the additional option to specify the mount speed used for the microSD (using <a href="#file_mountspeed">file_MountSpeed</a>)</p>
<p>Any memory allocations in the main FLASH program are released, however, the stack and globals are maintained. </p>
<p>The function 'main' in the called program accepts the arguments, if any. If arglistptr is 0, no arguments are passed, else arglistptr points to an array, the first element containing the number of additional elements in the array which contain the arguments.</p>
<p>The disk does not need to be mounted, file_Run automatically mounts the drive.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_RunSpeed(speed, fname, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">speed</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the speed. Speed can be from <code>SPI_SPEED0</code> (slowest) to <code>SPI_SPEED15</code> (fastest)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filename of the 4DGL child program to be loaded into RAM and executed</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<!-- TODO: Confirm if 'fname' accepts a string (byte-aligned) pointer or array (word-aligned) pointer -->

<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Value returned by main function in the called program</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<p>Refer to [#file_run] for an example.</p>
<h3 class="page-break" id="file_exec">file_Exec</h3>
<p>This function is similar to <a href="#file_run">file_Run</a>, however, the main program in FLASH retains all memory allocations (eg file buffers, memory allocated with mem_Alloc etc)</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_LoadFunction(fname);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filename of the 4DGL child program to be loaded into RAM and executed</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Value returned by main function in the called program</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl</h3>
<p>Reads a control file to create an image list.</p>
<p id="file_loadimagecontrol_modes">The following are the modes of operation</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Mode</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">It is assumed that there is a graphics file with the file extension "fname2.gci". In this case, the images have been stored in a FAT16 file concurrently, and the offsets that are derived from the "fname1.dat" file are saved in the image control so that the image control can open the file (*.gci) and use <a href="#file_seek">file_Seek(...)</a> to get to the position of the image which can then automatically be displayed using <a href="#file_image">file_Image(...)</a>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Mode 0 builds the image control quickly as it only scans the *.dat file for the file offsets and saves them in the relevant entries in the image control. The penalty is that images take longer to find when displayed due to <a href="#file_seek">file_Seek(...)</a> overheads.</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">It is assumed that there is a graphics file with the file extension "fname2.gci". In this case, the images have been stored in a FAT16 file concurrently, and the offset of the images are saved in the image control so that image file (*.gci) can be mapped to directly. The absolute cluster/sector is mapped so file seek does not need to be called internally. This means that there is no seek time penalty, however, the image list takes a lot longer to build, as all the seeking is done at control build time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">In this case, the images have been stored in a in a RAW partition of the uSD card, and the absolute address of the images are saved in the DAT file. This is the fastest operation of the image control as there is no seeking or other disk activity taking place.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">This mode is for Flash based 'file system' GCI (GCIF) with integrated DAT and other file types. "fname1" and "fname2" are then the Flash high and low words of the GCIF start location.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>When an image control is loaded, an array is built in RAM. It consists of a 6 word header with the following entries as defined by the constants:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Information</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Index</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_COUNT</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_ENTRYLEN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_MODE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_GCI_FILENAME</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_DAT_FILENAME</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">4</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_GCIFILE_HANDLE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">5</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>No images are stored in FLASH or RAM, the image control holds the index values for the absolute storage positions on the uSD card for RAW mode, or the cluster/sector position for formatted FAT16 mode.</p>
<p>When an image control is no longer required, the memory can be released with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free()</a>;</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_LoadImageControl(fname1, fname2, mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The control list filename "*.dat".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The image filename "*.gci".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Determines the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol_modes">mode of operation</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<!-- TODO: Confirm if 'fname1' and 'fname2' accept string (byte-aligned) pointer or array (word-aligned) pointer -->

<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Pointer (handle) to the memory allocation to the image control list that has been created, null (0) if function fails</p>

<h3 id="file_mount">file_Mount</h3>
<p>Starts up the FAT16 disk file services and allocates a small 32 byte control block for subsequent use. When you open a file using <a href="#file_open">file_Open(...)</a>, a further 512 + 44 = 556 bytes are attached to the FAT16 file control block. When you close a file using <a href="#file_close">file_Close(...)</a>, the 556 byte allocation is released leaving the 32 byte file control block. The <a href="#file_mount">file_Mount()</a> function must be called before any other FAT16 file related functions can be used. The control block and all FAT16 file resources are completely released with <a href="#file_unmount">file_Unmount()</a>. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_Mount();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: True (1) if successful, False (0) otherwise</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-41-1" name="__codelineno-41-1" href="#__codelineno-41-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">!</span><span class="n">file_Mount</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-41-2" name="__codelineno-41-2" href="#__codelineno-41-2"></a><span class="w">   </span><span class="k">while</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">file_Mount</span><span class="p">()))</span>
<a id="__codelineno-41-3" name="__codelineno-41-3" href="#__codelineno-41-3"></a><span class="w">      </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Disk not mounted"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-41-4" name="__codelineno-41-4" href="#__codelineno-41-4"></a><span class="w">      </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">200</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-41-5" name="__codelineno-41-5" href="#__codelineno-41-5"></a><span class="w">      </span><span class="n">gfx_Cls</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-41-6" name="__codelineno-41-6" href="#__codelineno-41-6"></a><span class="w">      </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">200</span><span class="p">);</span>

<a id="__codelineno-41-8" name="__codelineno-41-8" href="#__codelineno-41-8"></a><span class="n">endif</span><span class="w"> </span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This function is only available for use on the uSD based PmmC version.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_mountspeed">file_MountSpeed</h3>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_MountSpeed(speed);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">speed</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the speed. Speed can be from <code>SPI_SPEED0</code> (slowest) to <code>SPI_SPEED15</code> (fastest)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h3 id="file_playwav">file_PlayWAV</h3>
<p>Open the wav file, decode the header to set the appropriate wave player parameters and set off the playing of the file as a background process. See <a href="#sound-control-functions">Sound Control Functions</a> for additional play control functions.</p>
<p id="file_playwav_err_codes">This function may return the following values if unsuccessful:</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Error Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-7</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Insufficient memory available for WAV buffer and file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-6</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">cant play this rate</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-5</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no data chunk found in first rsector</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no format data</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no wave chunk signature</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">bad wave file format</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">file not found</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_PlayWAV(fname);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filename of the wav file to be opened and played</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<!-- TODO: Confirm if 'fname' accepts a string (byte-aligned) pointer or array (word-aligned) pointer -->

<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Number of blocks to play (1 to 32767), or <a href="#file_playwav_err_codes">error code</a> otherwise.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-44-1" name="__codelineno-44-1" href="#__codelineno-44-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">ding.wav</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_checkupdate">file_CheckUpdate</h3>
<p>Checks and/or updates the program running in Flash using the specified file on uSD.</p>
<p id="file_checkupdate_options">The following options determine the mode of operation:</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Option</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_QUERY</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Checks the specified file and compares its DateTime to the program running in Flash</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_UPDATENEWER</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Updates the program in Flash if the program on uSD is newer</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_UPDATEALWAYS</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Always updates the program in Flash</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p id="file_checkupdate_results">
If update occurs and the program is running from Flash, the display is reset after update.
Otherwise, if a query or an error occurs, the following is returned:
</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Option</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_NEWFILE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The specified file is newer than the file running in Flash</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_OLDFILE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The specified file is equal to or older than the file running in Flash</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_UPDATEDONE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">An update was performed, and the program is running from RAM</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_NOFILE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The specified file does not exist</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_INVALIDFILE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">5</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The specified file is not valid '4xe' or '4fn'</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_CheckUpdate(fname, options);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filename of the 4DGL program on the uSD card</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><a href="#file_checkupdate_options">options</a></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Determines whether to update always (3), update if newer (2) or simply query (1)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<!-- TODO: Confirm if 'fname' accepts a string (byte-aligned) pointer or array (word-aligned) pointer -->

<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: <a href="#file_checkupdate_results">Result of the operation</a></p>
<p class="page-break"></p>

<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-45-1" name="__codelineno-45-1" href="#__codelineno-45-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">file_Mount</span><span class="p">()))</span>

<a id="__codelineno-45-4" name="__codelineno-45-4" href="#__codelineno-45-4"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">200</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h2 class="page-break" id="general-purpose-functions">General Purpose Functions</h2>
<h3 id="lookup8">lookup8</h3>
<p>Search a list of 8-bit constant values for a match with a search value 'key'. If found, the index of the matching constant is returned. Thus, if the value is found first in the list, result is set to one. If second in the list, result is set to two etc. If not found, result is zero.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>lookup8(key, ...byteConstList);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">key</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A byte value to search for in a fixed list of constants</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">byteConstList</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A comma separated list of constants and strings to be matched against 'key'</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Index/Position of the matching constant starting with 1. 0 if 'key' doesn't exist</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-52-1" name="__codelineno-52-1" href="#__codelineno-52-1"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">main</span><span class="p">()</span>
<a id="__codelineno-52-2" name="__codelineno-52-2" href="#__codelineno-52-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">r</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">key</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sc">'a'</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-52-3" name="__codelineno-52-3" href="#__codelineno-52-3"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">r</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">lookup8</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">key</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x4D</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"abcd"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sc">'Z'</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-52-4" name="__codelineno-52-4" href="#__codelineno-52-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">Search value 'a' </span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">found as index "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">r</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-52-5" name="__codelineno-52-5" href="#__codelineno-52-5"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-52-6" name="__codelineno-52-6" href="#__codelineno-52-6"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">key</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-52-7" name="__codelineno-52-7" href="#__codelineno-52-7"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">r</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">lookup8</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">key</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x4D</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"abcd"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sc">'Z'</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span>

<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>The list of constants cannot be re-directed.</li>
<li>This function offer a versatile way for returning an index for a given value. This can be very useful for data entry filtering and parameter input checking and wherever you need to check the validity of certain inputs.</li>

<h3 id="lookup16">lookup16</h3>
<p>Search a list of 16-bit constant values for a match with a search value 'key'. IIf found, the index of the matching constant is returned. Thus, if the value is found first in the list, result is set to one. If second in the list, result is set to two etc. If not found, result is zero. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>lookup16(key, wordConstList);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">key</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A word value to search for in a fixed list of constants</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">wordConstList</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A comma separated list of constants and strings to be matched against 'key'</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Index/Position of the matching constant starting with 1. 0 if 'key' doesn't exist</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="rect_intersect">rect_Intersect</h3>
<p>This function detects if two rectangles intersect each other or not. It is ideal for use as a collision detector.
Each rectangle is an array of four words in the format <code>[xpos, ypos, width, height]</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>rect_Intersect(&amp;rect1, &amp;rect2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>

<td style="text-align: left;">An array of 4 vars containing left, top, width and height values</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">rect2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">An array of 4 vars containing left, top, width and height values</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: True (1) if any part of rect1 is within rect2, False (0) otherwise</p>

<a id="__codelineno-57-2" name="__codelineno-57-2" href="#__codelineno-57-2"></a><span class="n">pin_Set</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">INPUT</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="c1">// set IO1 to be used as an input</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="pin_hi">pin_HI</h3>
<p>Outputs a "High" level (logic 1) on the appropriate pin that was previously selected as an Output. If the pin is not already set to an output, it is automatically made an output.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>pin_HI(pin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value (usually a constant) specifying the pin number</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-58-1" name="__codelineno-58-1" href="#__codelineno-58-1"></a><span class="n">pin_HI</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO2_PIN</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">        </span><span class="c1">// output a Logic 1 on IO2 pin</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="pin_lo">pin_LO</h3>
<p>Outputs a "Low" level (logic 0) on the appropriate pin that was previously selected as an output. If the pin is not yet set as an output, it is automatically made to an output.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>pin_LO(pin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value (usually a constant) specifying the pin number</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-59-1" name="__codelineno-59-1" href="#__codelineno-59-1"></a><span class="n">pin_LO</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">        </span><span class="c1">// output a Logic 0 on IO1 pin</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="pin_read">pin_Read</h3>
<p>Reads the logic state of the pin that was previously selected as an Input. If a digital input, this
returns a "Low" (logic 0) or "High" (logic 1). Otherwise, it returns a 12-bit analogue value</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>pin_Read(pin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value (usually a constant) specifying the pin number</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong></p>
<div class="tabbed-set tabbed-alternate" data-tabs="4:2" style="--md-indicator-x: 16px; --md-indicator-width: 68px;"><input checked="checked" id="__tabbed_4_1" name="__tabbed_4" type="radio"><input id="__tabbed_4_2" name="__tabbed_4" type="radio"><div class="tabbed-labels"><label for="__tabbed_4_1">Digital</label><label for="__tabbed_4_2">Analogue</label></div>
<div class="tabbed-content">
<div class="tabbed-block">
<p>A Logic 1 (0x0001) or Logic 0 (0x0000)</p>
</div>
<div class="tabbed-block">
<p>12-bit analogue value </p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="tabbed-control tabbed-control--prev" hidden=""><button class="tabbed-button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"></button></div><div class="tabbed-control tabbed-control--next" hidden=""><button class="tabbed-button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"></button></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-60-1" name="__codelineno-60-1" href="#__codelineno-60-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">pin_Read</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">==</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="c1">// read the value on IO1</span>
<a id="__codelineno-60-2" name="__codelineno-60-2" href="#__codelineno-60-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">calc_Threshold</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-60-3" name="__codelineno-60-3" href="#__codelineno-60-3"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="ow_reset">OW_Reset</h3>
<p>Resets an 1-wire device and returns the status</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>OW_Reset(pin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value (usually a constant) specifying the pin number</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Status of 1-wire device (0: ACK, 1: No Activity)</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-61-1" name="__codelineno-61-1" href="#__codelineno-61-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print a 0 if the device initialised successfully.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-61-2" name="__codelineno-61-2" href="#__codelineno-61-2"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"result="</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OW_Reset</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">));</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>All PIXXI-28 and PIXXI-44 pins are capable of 1-wire protocol.
Refer to these <a href="#pixxi_pins">tables</a> for the list of pins.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="ow_read">OW_Read</h3>
<p>Reads the 8-bit value from a 1-wire devices register</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>OW_Read(pin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value (usually a constant) specifying the pin number</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: the lower 8-bits contain data bits received from the 1-Wire device</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-62-1" name="__codelineno-62-1" href="#__codelineno-62-1"></a><span class="c1">// read temperature from DS1821 device</span>
<a id="__codelineno-62-2" name="__codelineno-62-2" href="#__codelineno-62-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">temp_buf</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-62-3" name="__codelineno-62-3" href="#__codelineno-62-3"></a><span class="n">OW_Reset</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">               </span><span class="c1">// reset the device</span>
<a id="__codelineno-62-4" name="__codelineno-62-4" href="#__codelineno-62-4"></a><span class="n">OW_Write</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xAA</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// send the read command</span>
<a id="__codelineno-62-5" name="__codelineno-62-5" href="#__codelineno-62-5"></a><span class="nl">temp_buf</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OW_Read</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// read the device register</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>All PIXXI-28 and PIXXI-44 pins are capable of 1-wire protocol.
Refer to these <a href="#pixxi_pins">tables</a> for the list of pins.</p>
</div>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-63-1" name="__codelineno-63-1" href="#__codelineno-63-1"></a><span class="c1">// read temperature from DS1821 device</span>
<a id="__codelineno-63-2" name="__codelineno-63-2" href="#__codelineno-63-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">temp_buf</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-63-3" name="__codelineno-63-3" href="#__codelineno-63-3"></a><span class="n">OW_Reset</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                </span><span class="c1">// reset the device</span>
<a id="__codelineno-63-4" name="__codelineno-63-4" href="#__codelineno-63-4"></a><span class="n">OW_Write</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mh">0xAA</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">           </span><span class="c1">// send the read command</span>
<a id="__codelineno-63-5" name="__codelineno-63-5" href="#__codelineno-63-5"></a><span class="nl">temp_buf</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OW_Read9</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// read the device register</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">

</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="ow_write">OW_Write</h3>
<p>Writes the 8-bit data to 1-Wire devices register.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>OW_Write(pin, value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value (usually a constant) specifying the pin number</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The lower 8-bits of data are sent to the 1-Wire device</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-64-1" name="__codelineno-64-1" href="#__codelineno-64-1"></a><span class="c1">//===================================================================</span>

<h3 id="joystick">joystick</h3>
<p>Returns the value of the joystick position (5 position switch implementation). The joystick values are:</p>
<p id="joystick_values"></p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Status</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">JOY_RELEASED</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">JOY_UP</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">JOY_LEFT</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">JOY_DOWN</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">JOY_RIGHT</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">5</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">JOY_BTNB</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">6</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">JOY_BTNA</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>The joystick input uses the speficied pin utilizing the A/D converter.
Refer to these <a href="#pixxi_pins">tables</a> for to determine the pins capable of ADC operation.</p>
<p>Each switch is connected to a junction of 2 resistors that form a unique voltage divider circuit.</p>
<p>The joystick can also be implemented using multiple buttons and resistors.
Refer to the <strong>Analog Input</strong> section of the <a href="../../../datasheets/pixxi28/processor/#analog-input">PIXXI-28</a>
and <a href="../../../datasheets/pixxi44/processor/#analog-input">PIXXI-44</a> processor datasheets for the required resistor values.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>joystick(pin);</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: <a href="#joystick_values">Joystick value</a></p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-65-1" name="__codelineno-65-1" href="#__codelineno-65-1"></a><span class="n">txt_MoveCursor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-65-2" name="__codelineno-65-2" href="#__codelineno-65-2"></a><span class="nl">joy</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">joystick</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="c1">// read the joystick on IO1</span>
<a id="__codelineno-65-3" name="__codelineno-65-3" href="#__codelineno-65-3"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">joy</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">==</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">JOY_RELEASED</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"         "</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="bus_in">bus_In</h3>
<p>Read the 7-bit port regardless of pin configurations. If a pin is configured as input, the pin is read directly as if it were a digital input. If a pin is configured as an output, the pin is also read directly, giving the output latch state.</p>
<p id="bus_bit_table"></p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Pin Name</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Pin Number</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">BUS Bit Number</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IO12_PIN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IO13_PIN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">8</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IO14_PIN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">9</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IO15_PIN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">10</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IO16_PIN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">11</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">4</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IO17_PIN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">12</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">5</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IO18_PIN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">44</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">6</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>bus_In();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: 7-bit value of the bus</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-66-1" name="__codelineno-66-1" href="#__codelineno-66-1"></a><span class="nl">var1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">bus_In</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Read the 7-bit value off the IO12-IO18 pins</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This is only available in Mode 2 (4-wire SPI Mode) of PIXXI-44</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="bus_out">bus_Out</h3>
<p>The lower 7 bits of the argument are placed on the 7bit wide bus. Any BUS pins that are set to inputs are not affected.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>bus_Out(value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value (usually a constant) specifying the pin number. Bit 0 corresponds to IO12 through to bit6 which corresponds to IO18. This is a 7-bit BUS.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-67-1" name="__codelineno-67-1" href="#__codelineno-67-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">arg1</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-67-2" name="__codelineno-67-2" href="#__codelineno-67-2"></a><span class="nl">arg1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mb">0b0011010</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// set desired mask</span>
<a id="__codelineno-67-3" name="__codelineno-67-3" href="#__codelineno-67-3"></a><span class="n">bus_Out</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">arg1</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// set IO13, IO15 and IO16 to output, making them HI</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This is only available in Mode 2 (4-wire SPI Mode) of PIXXI-44</p>
</div>
<h2 class="page-break" id="graphics-functions">Graphics Functions</h2>
<h3 id="gfx_cls">gfx_Cls</h3>
<p>Clear the screen using the current background colour. This brings some of the settings back to default, such as:</p>
<ul>
<li>Transparency turned OFF</li>
<li>Outline colour set to BLACK</li>
<li>Opacity set to OPAQUE</li>
<li>Pen set to OUTLINE</li>
<li>Line patterns set to OFF</li>
<li>Right text margin set to full width</li>
<li>Text magnifications set to 1</li>
<li>All origins set to 0:0</li>
</ul>
<p>The alternative to maintain settings and to clear screen is to draw a filled rectangle with the required background colour. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Cls();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-68-1" name="__codelineno-68-1" href="#__codelineno-68-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_BGcolour</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">DARKGRAY</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-68-2" name="__codelineno-68-2" href="#__codelineno-68-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Cls</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// clears the entire display using colour DARKGRAY </span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_changecolour">gfx_ChangeColour</h3>
<p>Changes all <strong>oldColour</strong> pixels to <strong>newColour</strong> within the clipping area. See <a href="#gfx_setclipregion">gfx_SetClipRegion(...)</a> and <a href="#gfx_clipwindow">gfx_ClipWindow(...)</a></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_ChangeColour(oldColour, newColour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">oldColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the sample colour to be changed within the clipping window</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">newColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the new colour to change all occurrences of <strong>oldColour</strong> within the clipping window</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-69-1" name="__codelineno-69-1" href="#__codelineno-69-1"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>
<a id="__codelineno-69-2" name="__codelineno-69-2" href="#__codelineno-69-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-69-3" name="__codelineno-69-3" href="#__codelineno-69-3"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">txt_Width</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                   </span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_circle">gfx_Circle</h3>
<p>Draws a circle with centre point x1, y1 with radius r using the specified colour.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Circle(x, y, radius, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the center of the circle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">radius</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the radius of the circle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the circle</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-70-1" name="__codelineno-70-1" href="#__codelineno-70-1"></a><span class="c1">// Draws a BLUE circle outline (assuming PEN_SIZE is OUTLINE)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-70-2" name="__codelineno-70-2" href="#__codelineno-70-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Circle</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RED</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// centred at x=50, y=50 with a radius of 30 pixel units</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The default <code>PEN_SIZE</code> is set to <code>OUTLINE</code>, however, if <code>PEN_SIZE</code> is set to <code>SOLID</code>,
the circle will be drawn filled, if <code>PEN_SIZE</code> is set to <code>OUTLINE</code>, the circle will be drawn as an outline.
If the circle is drawn as SOLID, the outline colour can be specified with
<a href="#gfx_outlinecolour">gfx_OutlineColour(...)</a>. If <code>OUTLINE_COLOUR</code> is set to 0, no outline is drawn. </p>
</div>

<h3 id="gfx_line">gfx_Line</h3>
<p>Draws a line from x1, y1 to x2, y2 using the specified colour. The line is drawn using the current object colour.
The current origin is not altered. The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Line(x1, y1, x2, y2, colour);</code></p>

</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the ending coordinates of the line</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the line</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
