<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_roundrect">gfx_RoundRect</h3>
<p>Draw a filled rectangle at the given co-ordinates with optional rounded corners.</p>
<p>If x1 = x2 or y1 = y2 no straight-line part is drawn. </p>
<p><img alt="gfx_RoundRect Diagram" src="../img/pixxi/gfx_roundrect.jpg"></p>
<p>The actual width of the round-corners rectangle is computed by: <code>2 * rad + x2 – x1</code></p>
<p>The actual height of the round-corners rectangle is computed by: <code>2 * rad + y2 – y1</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_RoundRect(x1, y1, x2, y2, rad, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner of the <strong>inner</strong> rectangle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the bottom right corner of the <strong>inner</strong> rectangle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">rad</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the radius of corners<br>This is the distance in pixels extending from the corners of the <strong>inner</strong> rectangle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the rectangle</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-77-1" name="__codelineno-77-1" href="#__codelineno-77-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_RoundRect</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">80</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">80</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RED</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_polyline">gfx_Polyline</h3>
<p>Plots lines between points specified by a pair of arrays using the specified colour.
The lines may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function.
This can be used to create complex raster graphics by loading the arrays from serial input or from MEDIA with very little code requirement.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Polyline(n, vx, vy, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">n</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of elements in the x and y arrays specifying the vertices for the polyline</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vx</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the x coordinates of the vertices</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vy</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the y coordinates of the vertices</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour for the lines</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-78-1" name="__codelineno-78-1" href="#__codelineno-78-1"></a><span class="cp">#inherit "4DGL_16bitColours.fnc"</span>
<a id="__codelineno-78-2" name="__codelineno-78-2" href="#__codelineno-78-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-78-3" name="__codelineno-78-3" href="#__codelineno-78-3"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">vx</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">vy</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">];</span>
<a id="__codelineno-78-4" name="__codelineno-78-4" href="#__codelineno-78-4"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-78-5" name="__codelineno-78-5" href="#__codelineno-78-5"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>

<a id="__codelineno-78-50" name="__codelineno-78-50" href="#__codelineno-78-50"></a><span class="n">endfunc</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="gfx_polygon">gfx_Polygon</h3>
<p>Plots lines between points specified by a pair of arrays using the specified colour.
The last point is drawn back to the first point, completing the polygon.
The lines may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function. 
This can be used to create complex raster graphics by loading the arrays from serial input or from MEDIA with very little code requirement.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Polygon(n, vx, vy, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">n</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of elements in the x and y arrays specifying the vertices for the polygon</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vx</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the x coordinates of the vertices</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vy</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the y coordinates of the vertices</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour for the polygon</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-79-1" name="__codelineno-79-1" href="#__codelineno-79-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">vx</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">7</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">vy</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">7</span><span class="p">];</span>

<h3 id="gfx_triangle">gfx_Triangle</h3>
<p>Draws a triangle outline between vertices (x1, y1), (x2, y2) and (x3, y3) using the specified colour.
The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Triangle(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the first vertices of the triangle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the second vertices of the triangle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x3, y3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the third vertices of the triangle</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-80-1" name="__codelineno-80-1" href="#__codelineno-80-1"></a><span class="c1">// Draws a CYAN triangular outline with vertices  at (10, 10), (30, 10) and (20, 30)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-80-2" name="__codelineno-80-2" href="#__codelineno-80-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Triangle</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">CYAN</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="gfx_dot">gfx_Dot</h3>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Dot();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-81-2" name="__codelineno-81-2" href="#__codelineno-81-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">40</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_bullet">gfx_Bullet</h3>
<p>Draws a <strong>circle</strong> or 'bullet point' with radius r at at the current origin using the current object colour.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Bullet(radius);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">radius</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the radius of the bullet</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-82-1" name="__codelineno-82-1" href="#__codelineno-82-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-82-2" name="__codelineno-82-2" href="#__codelineno-82-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Bullet</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Draw a 10pixel radius Bullet at x=30, y=30.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The default <code>PEN_SIZE</code> is set to <code>OUTLINE</code>, however, if <code>PEN_SIZE</code> is set to <code>SOLID</code>, the circle will be drawn filled,
if <code>PEN_SIZE</code> is set to <code>OUTLINE</code>, the circle will be drawn as an outline.
If the circle is drawn as <code>SOLID</code>, the outline colour can be specified with <a href="#gfx_outlinecolour">gfx_OutlineColour(...)</a></p>
</div>
<h3 id="gfx_orbitinit">gfx_OrbitInit</h3>
<p>Sets up the internal pointers for the <a href="#gfx_orbit">gfx_Orbit(..)</a> result variables.
The &amp;x_orb and &amp;y_orb parameters are the addresses of the variables or array elements
that are used to store the result from the <a href="#gfx_orbit">gfx_Orbit(..)</a> function. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_OrbitInit(&amp;x_dest, &amp;y_dest);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;x_dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the address of storage location of the X value for the orbit calculation</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;y_dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the address of storage location of the Y value for the orbit calculation</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-83-1" name="__codelineno-83-1" href="#__codelineno-83-1"></a><span class="c1">// Sets the variables that will receive the result from a gfx_Orbit(...) function call</span>
<a id="__codelineno-83-2" name="__codelineno-83-2" href="#__codelineno-83-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-83-3" name="__codelineno-83-3" href="#__codelineno-83-3"></a><span class="n">gfx_OrbitInit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="gfx_orbit">gfx_Orbit</h3>
<p>Prior to using this function, the destination address of variables for the calculated
coordinates must be set using the <a href="#gfx_orbitinit">gfx_OrbitInit(...)</a> function.
This function calculates the x, y coordinates of a distant point relative to the current origin,
where the only known parameters are the angle and the distance from the current origin.
The new coordinates are calculated and then placed in the destination variables that
have been previously set with the <a href="#gfx_orbitinit">gfx_OrbitInit(...)</a> function. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Orbit(angle, distance);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">angle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the angle from the origin to the remote point. The angle is specified in degrees.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">distance</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the distance from the origin to the remote point in pixel units</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-84-1" name="__codelineno-84-1" href="#__codelineno-84-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-84-2" name="__codelineno-84-2" href="#__codelineno-84-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_OrbitInit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-84-3" name="__codelineno-84-3" href="#__codelineno-84-3"></a><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-84-4" name="__codelineno-84-4" href="#__codelineno-84-4"></a><span class="n">gfx_Bullet</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="c1">// mark the start point with a small WHITE circle</span>
<a id="__codelineno-84-5" name="__codelineno-84-5" href="#__codelineno-84-5"></a><span class="n">gfx_Orbit</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// calculate a point 50 pixels away from origin at</span>
<a id="__codelineno-84-6" name="__codelineno-84-6" href="#__codelineno-84-6"></a><span class="w">                   </span><span class="c1">// 30 degrees</span>
<a id="__codelineno-84-7" name="__codelineno-84-7" href="#__codelineno-84-7"></a><span class="c1">// mark the target point with a RED circle</span>
<a id="__codelineno-84-8" name="__codelineno-84-8" href="#__codelineno-84-8"></a><span class="n">gfx_CircleFilled</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">targetX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">targetY</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xF800</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Result is stored in the variables that were specified with the <a href="#gfx_orbitinit">gfx_OrbitInit(...)</a> function.</p>
</div>

<h3 id="gfx_lineto">gfx_LineTo</h3>
<p>Draws a line from the current origin to a new position.
The Origin is then set to the new position.
The line is drawn using the current object colour.
The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_LineTo(xpos, ypos);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xpos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal position of the line end as well as the new origin</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ypos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the vertical position of the line end as well as the new origin</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-91-1" name="__codelineno-91-1" href="#__codelineno-91-1"></a><span class="c1">// Draws a line using the current object colour between x1=10, y1=20 and x2=60, y2=70.</span>

<a id="__codelineno-91-4" name="__codelineno-91-4" href="#__codelineno-91-4"></a><span class="c1">// The new origin is now set at x=60, y=70.</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_linerel">gfx_LineRel</h3>

<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal end point of the line</td>

<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ypos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the vertical end point of the line</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_boxto">gfx_BoxTo</h3>
<p>Draws a rectangle from the current origin to the new point using the current object colour.
The top left corner is anchored by the current origin (x1, y1), the bottom right corner is specified by x2, y2.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_BoxTo(x2, y2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the diagonally opposed corner of the rectangle to be drawn, the top left corner (assumed to be x1, y1) is anchored by the current origin.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>

<a id="__codelineno-93-8" name="__codelineno-93-8" href="#__codelineno-93-8"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">gfx_BoxTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">);</span>

<a id="__codelineno-93-10" name="__codelineno-93-10" href="#__codelineno-93-10"></a><span class="n">wend</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The default <code>PEN_SIZE</code> is set to <code>OUTLINE</code>, however, if <code>PEN_SIZE</code> is set to <code>SOLID</code>,
the rectangle will be drawn filled, if <code>PEN_SIZE</code> is set to <code>OUTLINE</code>, the rectangle
will be drawn as an outline. If the circle is drawn as <code>SOLID</code>, the outline colour
can be specified with <a href="#gfx_outlinecolour">gfx_OutlineColour(...)</a>.
If <code>OUTLINE_COLOUR</code> is set to 0, no outline is drawn. </p>
</div>

<h3 id="gfx_setclipregion">gfx_SetClipRegion</h3>
<p>Forces the clip region to the most recent extents. It can be the extents of the last text that was printed or the last image that was shown.</p>
<p>For the clipping region to take effect, "Clipping" setting must be enabled separately using <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Set(CLIPPING, ON)</a> or the shortcut <a href="#gfx_clipping">gfx_Clipping(ON)</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_SetClipRegion();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_clipwindow">gfx_ClipWindow</h3>
<p>Specifies a clipping window region on the screen such that any objects and text placed onto the screen will be clipped and displayed only within that region. </p>
<p>For the clipping window to take effect, "Clipping" setting must be enabled separately using  <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Set(CLIPPING, ON)</a> or the shortcut <a href="#gfx_clipping">gfx_Clipping(ON)</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_ClipWindow(x1, y1, x2, y2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the top left corner of the clipping window</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the bottom right corner of the clipping window</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-103-1" name="__codelineno-103-1" href="#__codelineno-103-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">n</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-103-2" name="__codelineno-103-2" href="#__codelineno-103-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_ClipWindow</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-103-3" name="__codelineno-103-3" href="#__codelineno-103-3"></a><span class="n">gfx_Clipping</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ON</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-103-4" name="__codelineno-103-4" href="#__codelineno-103-4"></a><span class="nl">n</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50000</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-103-5" name="__codelineno-103-5" href="#__codelineno-103-5"></a><span class="k">while</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="o">--</span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-103-6" name="__codelineno-103-6" href="#__codelineno-103-6"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// Draw 50000 random colour pixels,</span>
<a id="__codelineno-103-7" name="__codelineno-103-7" href="#__codelineno-103-7"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// only the pixels within the clipping area will be visible</span>
<a id="__codelineno-103-8" name="__codelineno-103-8" href="#__codelineno-103-8"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">gfx_PutPixel</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="o">%</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="o">%</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">());</span>
<a id="__codelineno-103-9" name="__codelineno-103-9" href="#__codelineno-103-9"></a><span class="n">wend</span>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_get">gfx_Get</h3>
<p>Returns various graphics parameters to caller.</p>
<p>The following graphics parameters can be queried:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Mode</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>X_MAX</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Current orientations maximum X Value</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>Y_MAX</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Current orientations maximum Y Value</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>LEFT_POS</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Left location of Object</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>TOP_POS</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Top location of Object</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>RIGHT_POS</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Right location of Object</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>BOTTOM_POS</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bottom location of Object</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>X_ORG</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Get current internal X position</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>Y_ORG</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Get current internal Y position</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Get(mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies graphics parameter to query</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: the value of the parameter being queried</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-104-1" name="__codelineno-104-1" href="#__codelineno-104-1"></a><span class="nl">val</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">gfx_Get</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">X_MAX</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="c1">// Returns the maximum horizontal resolution of the display</span>
<a id="__codelineno-104-2" name="__codelineno-104-2" href="#__codelineno-104-2"></a><span class="nl">val</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">gfx_Get</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">Y_MAX</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="c1">// Returns the maximum vertical resolution of the display</span>
<a id="__codelineno-104-3" name="__codelineno-104-3" href="#__codelineno-104-3"></a><span class="nl">val</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">gfx_Get</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">RIGHT_POS</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// Returns the right location of the last drawn object</span>
<a id="__codelineno-104-4" name="__codelineno-104-4" href="#__codelineno-104-4"></a><span class="w">                            </span><span class="c1">// that only has top, left parameters such as a button</span>
<a id="__codelineno-104-5" name="__codelineno-104-5" href="#__codelineno-104-5"></a><span class="w">                            </span><span class="c1">// or an image/video.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-104-6" name="__codelineno-104-6" href="#__codelineno-104-6"></a><span class="nl">val</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">gfx_Get</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BOTTOM_POS</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Returns the bottom location of the last drawn object</span>
<a id="__codelineno-104-7" name="__codelineno-104-7" href="#__codelineno-104-7"></a><span class="w">                            </span><span class="c1">// that only has top, left parameters such as a button</span>
<a id="__codelineno-104-8" name="__codelineno-104-8" href="#__codelineno-104-8"></a><span class="w">                            </span><span class="c1">// or an image/video.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_set">gfx_Set</h3>
<p>Set the required graphics control parameter, such as size, colour, and other parameters</p>
<p>The following parameters can be set</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Mode</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Value</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PEN_SIZE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set the draw mode for <a href="#gfx_lineto">gfx_LineTo</a>, <a href="#gfx_linerel">gfx_LineRel</a>, <a href="#gfx_dot">gfx_Dot</a>, <a href="#gfx_bullet">gfx_Bullet</a> and <a href="#gfx_boxto">gfx_BoxTo</a> (default mode is OUTLINE)</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 or <strong>SOLID</strong><br>1 or <strong>OUTLINE</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">BACKGROUND_COLOUR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set the screen background colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">16-bit Colour, 0x0000-0xFFFF</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OBJECT_COLOUR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Generic colour for <a href="#gfx_lineto">gfx_LineTo</a>, <a href="#gfx_linerel">gfx_LineRel</a>, <a href="#gfx_dot">gfx_Dot</a>, <a href="#gfx_bullet">gfx_Bullet</a> and <a href="#gfx_boxto">gfx_BoxTo</a></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">16-bit Colour, 0x0000-0xFFFF</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">CLIPPING</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Turns clipping on/off<br>The clipping points are set with <a href="#gfx_clipwindow">gfx_ClipWindow</a> and must be set first.</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1 or 0 (ON or OFF)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">TRANSPARENT_COLOUR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Colour that needs to be made transparent.</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">16-bit Colour, 0x0000-0xFFFF</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">TRANSPARENCY</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Turn the transparency ON or OFF. Transparency is automatically turned OFF after the next image or video command.</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1 or 0 (ON or OFF)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">FRAME_DELAY</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set the inter frame delay for <a href="#media_video">media_Video(...)</a></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 to 255msec</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">SCREEN_MODE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set required screen behaviour/orientation.</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 or <strong>LANDSCAPE</strong><br>1 or <strong>LANDSCAPE_R</strong><br>2 or <strong>PORTRAIT</strong><br>3 or <strong>PORTRAIT_R</strong><br></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OUTLINE_COLOUR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Outline colour for rectangles and circles<br>(set to 0 for no effect)</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">16-bit Colour, 0x0000-0xFFFF</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">CONTRAST</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set contrast value, 0 = display off, 1-15 = contrast level</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 or <strong>OFF</strong><br>1 to 15 for levels</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">BEVEL_WIDTH</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set Button Bevel Width, 0 pixel to 15 pixels.</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 None<br>1 to 15 pixels</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Set(function, value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">function</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Determines the required action for various graphics control functions. There are pre-defined constants for each of the functions</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Target new setting/value for the target display function</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_readgramarea">gfx_ReadGRAMarea</h3>
<p>Reads an arbitrary rectangular area from the display to an array.
If "ptr" is 0, the correctly sized array is created, in which case it is up to the caller to eventually destroy it.
Otherwise "ptr" is expected to point to a correctly sized array.</p>
<p>If an array is supplied, its size must be large enough, and may be calculated:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>bytecount = (ABS(x2 - x1) + 1) * (ABS(y2 - y1) + 1)</code></li>
<li><code>wordcount = 2 * bytecount</code></li>
</ul>
<p><em>*bytecount can be used when creating a buffer using <a href="#mem_alloc">mem_Alloc</a></em></p>
<p><em>*wordcount can be used when creating a fixed <strong>var</strong> array</em></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_ReadGRAMarea(x1, y1, x2, y2, ptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Top left corner of the rectangular area</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bottom right corner of the rectangular area</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to an array large enought to store each pixel or;<br>0 to automatically create an array of the required size</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li>If <code>ptr</code> is 0, returns the created array if there is insufficient memory, otherwise, returns 0</li>
<li>If <code>ptr</code> is nonzero, returns the user's array <code>ptr</code></li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-106-1" name="__codelineno-106-1" href="#__codelineno-106-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">array</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-2" name="__codelineno-106-2" href="#__codelineno-106-2"></a><span class="nl">array</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">gfx_ReadGRAMarea</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">250</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">175</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-3" name="__codelineno-106-3" href="#__codelineno-106-3"></a><span class="c1">// Copy the pixels of the GRAM area with top left and bottom right </span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-4" name="__codelineno-106-4" href="#__codelineno-106-4"></a><span class="c1">// endpoints at (50,50) and (250,175) and saves it to the generated </span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-5" name="__codelineno-106-5" href="#__codelineno-106-5"></a><span class="c1">// array. The address is then returned and saved to variable ‘array’</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-6" name="__codelineno-106-6" href="#__codelineno-106-6"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-106-7" name="__codelineno-106-7" href="#__codelineno-106-7"></a><span class="n">gfx_BGcolour</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">LIME</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-8" name="__codelineno-106-8" href="#__codelineno-106-8"></a><span class="n">gfx_Cls</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Sets the background to a single color</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-9" name="__codelineno-106-9" href="#__codelineno-106-9"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-106-10" name="__codelineno-106-10" href="#__codelineno-106-10"></a><span class="n">gfx_WriteGRAMarea</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">300</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">225</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">array</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-11" name="__codelineno-106-11" href="#__codelineno-106-11"></a><span class="c1">// Copies the GRAM area to the new coordinates,</span>
<a id="__codelineno-106-12" name="__codelineno-106-12" href="#__codelineno-106-12"></a><span class="c1">// Top left and bottom right corners are at (100,100) and (300,225)</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 id="gfx_surround">gfx_Surround</h3>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Surround(x1, y1, x2, y2, rad1, rad2, colour);</code></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_roundgradient">gfx_RoundGradient</h3>
<p>Draws a graduated colour rounded rectangle at the specified co-ordinate. </p>
<p><strong>x1</strong> and <strong>y1</strong> may equal <strong>x2</strong> and <strong>y2</strong> allowing the function to be used for rounded panels, rounded buttons, circular buttons. </p>
<p><img alt="gfx_RoundGradient" src="../img/pixxi/gfx_roundrect.jpg"></p>
<p>Bounding rectangle is <strong>x1-radius</strong>, <strong>y1-radius</strong>, <strong>x2+radius</strong>, <strong>y2+radius</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_RoundGradient(style, x1, y1, x2, y2, radius, colour1, colour2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">style</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the gradient style</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner of the <strong>inner</strong> rectangle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the bottom right corner of the <strong>inner</strong> rectangle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">radius</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the radius of corners<br>This is the distance in pixels extending from the corners of the <strong>inner</strong> rectangle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the start colour of the gradient</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the end colour of the gradient</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-109-1" name="__codelineno-109-1" href="#__codelineno-109-1"></a><span class="c1">// Draw graduated colour rounded rectangle</span>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_xyrottoval">gfx_XYrotToVal</h3>
<p>This function converts a rotational angle into a value. It calculates a position for a rotary
input starting at <strong>mina</strong> and continuing to <strong>maxa</strong>. Both angles must be greater than 0.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_XYrotToVal(x, y, base, mina, maxa, minv, maxv);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Relative x-coordinate (x-coordinate – x-center)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Relative y-coordinate (y-coordinate – y-center)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">base</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The base reference at which the angle is 0<br><code>XYROT_EAST</code> angle 0 starts from the east<br><code>XYROT_SOUTH</code> angle 0 starts from the south</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mina</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Start angle (Clockwise from 0 angle)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">maxa</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">End angle (Clockwise from 0 angle)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">minv</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Minimum value</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">maxv</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Maximum value</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: The equivalent position, the value of which will be between <strong>minv</strong> and <strong>maxv</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-110-1" name="__codelineno-110-1" href="#__codelineno-110-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">pos</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-110-2" name="__codelineno-110-2" href="#__codelineno-110-2"></a><span class="nl">pos</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">gfx_XYrotToVal</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">150</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">150</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">-</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">XYROT_EAST</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">180</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-110-3" name="__codelineno-110-3" href="#__codelineno-110-3"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">pos</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Prints value of 25, expected at angle of 45 degrees</span>
<a id="__codelineno-110-4" name="__codelineno-110-4" href="#__codelineno-110-4"></a><span class="w">            </span><span class="c1">// with the origin at x = 100, y = 100</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_spriteset">gfx_SpriteSet</h3>
<p>This function sets the internal pointers for the 3 sets of data required by the sprite generator which are as follows:
1. the bitmaps for the sprites
2. the colour lookup table (CLUT)
3. the 4 colour palettes</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_SpriteSet(bitmaps, colours, palette);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bitmaps</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to bitmaps</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colours</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to colour lookup table</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">palette</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the 4 colour palettes</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>

<h3 id="gfx_blitsprite">gfx_BlitSprite</h3>

Orientation determines in which direction the sprite will be displayed. If preimage exists,
it should be large enough to hold the entire image 'underneath' the sprite.</p>

<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">SOUTH</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">WEST</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">EAST</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">NORTH_MIRRORED</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">4</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">SOUTH_MIRRORED</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">5</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">WEST_MIRRORED</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">6</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">EAST_MIRRORED</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">7</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_BlitSprite(spritenumber, palette, xpos, ypos, orientation, preimage);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_button">gfx_Button</h3>
<p>Draws a three-dimensional Text Button at screen location defined by x, y parameters (top left corner).
The size of the button depends on the font, width, height and length of the text.</p>
<p>The button can contain multiple lines of text by having the <code>\n</code> character embedded in the string for the end of line marker. In this case, the widest text in the string sets the overall width, and the height of the button is set by the number of text lines. In the case of multiple lines, each line is left justified.</p>
<p>If you wish to centre or right justify the text, you will need to prepare the text string according to your requirements.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Button(state, x, y, buttonColour, txtColour, font, txtWidth txtHeight, text);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">state</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 = Button depressed; 1 = Button raised</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner position of the button on the screen</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buttonColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Button colour</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">txtColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Text colour</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">font</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the Font ID</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">txtWidth</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the width of the text. This value is the font width multiplier and minimum value must be 1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">txtHeight</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the height of the text. This value is the font height multiplier and minimum value must be 1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">text</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the text string. The text string must be within the range of printable ascii character set. The string may have \n characters embedded to create a multiline button</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_slider">gfx_Slider</h3>
<p>Draws a vertical or horizontal slider bar on the screen. The gfx_Slider function has several different modes of operation. To minimise the amount of graphics functions we need; all modes of operation are selected naturally depending on the parameter values.</p>
<p>Orientation Selection Rules:</p>
<ul>
<li>if x2-x1 &gt; y2-y1, slider is assumed to be horizontal (ie: if width &gt; height, slider is horizontal)</li>
<li>if x2-x1 &lt;= y2-y1, slider is assumed to be vertical (ie: if height &lt;= width, slider is horizontal)</li>
</ul>
<p>Thumb Selection Rules:</p>
<ul>
<li>If value is positive, thumb is set to the position that is the proportion of value to the scale parameter. (Used to set the control to the actual value of a variable)</li>
<li>If value is negative, thumb is driven to the graphics position set by the ABSolute of value. (Used to set thumb to its actual graphical position (usually by touch screen)</li>
<li>The thumb colour is determine by <code>gfx_Set(OBJECT_COLOUR, value);</code>, however, if the current object colour is BLACK, a darkened shade of the colour parameter is used for the thumb.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Slider(mode, x1, y1, x2, y2, colour, scale, value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>0</strong> : Slider Indented<br><strong>1</strong> : Slider Raised<br><strong>2</strong> : Slider Hidden (background colour)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner position of the slider on the screen</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the bottom right corner position of the slider on the screen</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the slider bar</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">scale</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the full range of the slider for the thumb from 0 to this value</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">if positive, sets the relative position of the thumb on the slider bar,<br>else set thumb to ABS position of the negative number</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li>If the value parameter was a positive number (i.e:- value is a proportion of the scale parameter), the true (implied x or y axis) position of the thumb is returned.</li>
<li>If the value parameter was a negative number (i.e:- thumb is being set to an Absolute graphics position), the actual slider value (which is a proportion of the scale parameter) is returned.</li>
</ul>
<p class="page-break"></p>

<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Dial(value, &amp;DialRam, &amp;DialDef);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value (usually a constant) specifying the current frame of the widget</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;DialRam</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A pointer to a variable array for widget utilization</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;DialDef</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A pointer to the Data Block holding the widget parameters</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_led">gfx_Led</h3>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_leddigit">gfx_LedDigit</h3>
<p>Draws a single 7 segment led Digit at x, y of size digitsize using oncolour and offcolour.
By default, the value can be 0-9 (0-9), A-F (0x0a-0x0f), blank(0x10) and - (0x11).</p>
<p>Additional options can be used in <strong>value</strong> as described in the table:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Options</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Bit/Flag</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LEDDIGIT_F_DP_COMMA</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0400</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Uses a comma as the decimal point</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LEDDIGIT_F_SHOW_DP</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0800</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Adds a decimal point to the value displayed</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LEDDIGIT_F_SET_SEGMENTS</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x1000</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Allows segments to be individually set</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<!--
TODO: Check LEDDIGIT_F_DP_ON and LEDDIGIT_F_SHOW_DP
    - Does LEDDIGIT_F_DP_ON turn the Decimal Point as Dot?
    - What happens if neither LEDDIGIT_F_DP_ON or LEDDIGIT_F_DP_COMMA was used? 
| LEDDIGIT_F_DP_ON          | 0x0200    | Uses a dot as the decimal point                       |
  -->

<p><code>LEDDIGIT_F_SET_SEGMENTS</code> can be used to turn value into a series of bits to turn on individual segments.
For example, <code>LEDDIGIT_F_SET_SEGMENTS + 9</code> will turn ON the top and bottom segments.</p>
<p>In this mode, <code>LEDDIGIT_F_SHOW_DP</code> and <code>LEDDIGIT_F_DP_COMMA</code> can be used, but in this case the DP is the 8th segment.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_LedDigit(x, y, digitsize, oncolour, offcolour, value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top-left position of the digit</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">digitsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the size of the digit</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">oncolour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the active colour of the segments/LEDs</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">offcolour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the inactive colour of the segments/LEDs</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the value to show</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-125-1" name="__codelineno-125-1" href="#__codelineno-125-1"></a><span class="c1">// Show 3 in the 7-segment LED digit</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_panel">gfx_Panel</h3>
<p>Draws a 3-dimensional rectangular panel at a screen location defined by x, y parameters (top left corner).
The size of the panel is set with the width and height parameters.
The colour is defined by colour.
The state parameter determines the appearance of the panel, 0 = recessed, 1 = raised.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_Panel(state, x, y, width, height, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">state</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>0</strong> : Recessed<br><strong>1</strong> : Raised</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner position of the panel on the screen</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">width</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the width of the panel</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">height</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the height of the panel</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the panel</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_gradientshape">gfx_GradientShape</h3>
<p>Produce a shaped color gradient using the supplied parameters
This function requires a quantity of RAM to work which needs to be initialised beforehand as a global array.
It's size varies according to the largest corner radius.
When initializing the format below can be used:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0">var gradientRAM[29 + xxx * 2] := [-1,-1, -9999, 0, 0, xxx];
</code></pre></div>
<p>where <code>xxx</code> is maximum radius + 1</p>
<p>For example: <code>gradientRAM[29+91*2] := [-1, -1, -9999, 0, 0, 91];</code></p>
<p>This can support a maximum radius of 90 pixels. <em>Notice the 91 in two places.</em></p>
<p>Multiple gradient shape calls can share the same GradientRAM.</p>
<!-- TODO: confirm value of xxx -->

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>gfx_GradientShape(GradientRAM, HorzVert, OuterWidth, X, Y, W, H, TLrad, TRrad, BLrad, BRrad, Darken, OuterColor, OuterType, OuterLevel, InnerColor, InnerType, InnerLevel, Split);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">GradientRAM</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">RAM buffer initialized to use for rendering gradient shapes</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">HorzVert</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>0</strong> : Horizontal<br><strong>1</strong> : Vertical</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OuterWidth</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Outer gradient width</td>

<h2 class="page-break" id="i2c-master-functions">I2C Master Functions</h2>
<h3 id="i2cx_open">I2Cx_Open</h3>
<p>This function configures the I2C module and initialises it to be ready.
The I2C clock <strong>speed</strong> is specified by the speed parameter.
Three I2C Speed settings are available to suit various requirements.</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;"></th>
<th style="text-align: center;">I2C Pin</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">PIXXI-28 Pin</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">PIXXI-44 Pin</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>I2C1 Bus</strong></td>
<td style="text-align: center;">SCL1</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">38</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;"></td>
<td style="text-align: center;">SDA1</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">37</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>I2C2 Bus</strong></td>
<td style="text-align: center;">SCL2</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">NA</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">25</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;"></td>
<td style="text-align: center;">SDA2</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">NA</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">27</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>I2C3 Bus</strong></td>
<td style="text-align: center;">SCL3</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">19</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;"></td>
<td style="text-align: center;">SDA3</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">12</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">42</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p id="i2cx_open_speed_constants">The following are the available speed options:</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Constant</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Speed</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_SLOW</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">100 kHz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_MED</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">400 kHz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_FAST</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1 MHz</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This functions is available for all 3 I2C buses of PIXXI-44 and 2 I2C buses of PIXXI-28.
The functions are prepended with <code>I2Cx</code> where x is 1 to 3.
This represents the bus number and can be checked from the display and processor datasheets.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>I2C1_Open(Speed);</code> or <code>I2C2_Open(Speed);</code> or <code>I2C3_Open(Speed);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Speed</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the I2C bus <a href="#i2cx_open_speed_constants">speed</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="i2cx_close">I2Cx_Close</h3>
<p>Calling this function closes the I2C port and disables the I2C hardware</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>

This represents the bus number and can be checked from the display and processor datasheets.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>I2C1_Close();</code> or <code>I2C2_Close();</code> or <code>I2C3_Close();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-133-1" name="__codelineno-133-1" href="#__codelineno-133-1"></a><span class="n">I2C1_Close</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Close I2C1 port and Disable the hardware</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="i2cx_start">I2Cx_Start</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends an I2C start condition.
The hardware first pulls the SDA (data) line low, and next pulls the SCL (clock) line low.</p>
<p><img alt="Start Condition" src="../img/pixxi/i2c-start.jpg"></p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This functions is available for all 3 I2C buses of PIXXI-44 and 2 I2C buses of PIXXI-28.
The functions are prepended with <code>I2Cx</code> where x is 1 to 3.
This represents the bus number and can be checked from the display and processor datasheets.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>I2C1_Start();</code> or <code>I2C2_Start();</code> or <code>I2C3_Start();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-134-1" name="__codelineno-134-1" href="#__codelineno-134-1"></a><span class="n">I2C1_Start</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Send an I2C start condition</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="i2cx_stop">I2Cx_Stop</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends an I2C stop condition. The hardware first releases the SCL to high state, and then releases the SDA line high.</p>
<p><img alt="Stop Condition" src="../img/pixxi/i2c-stop.jpg"></p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This functions is available for all 3 I2C buses of PIXXI-44 and 2 I2C buses of PIXXI-28.
The functions are prepended with <code>I2Cx</code> where x is 1 to 3.
This represents the bus number and can be checked from the display and processor datasheets.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>I2C1_Stop();</code> or <code>I2C2_Stop();</code> or <code>I2C3_Stop();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-135-1" name="__codelineno-135-1" href="#__codelineno-135-1"></a><span class="n">I2C1_Stop</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Send an I2C stop condition</span>

</div>

<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-136-1" name="__codelineno-136-1" href="#__codelineno-136-1"></a><span class="n">I2C1_Restart</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Generates an I2C restart condition</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="i2cx_read">I2Cx_Read</h3>
<p>Calling this function reads a single byte from the I2C bus</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>Data can only change when the clock is low.</li>
<li>This functions is available for all 3 I2C buses of PIXXI-44 and 2 I2C buses of PIXXI-28.
    The functions are prepended with <code>I2Cx</code> where x is 1 to 3.
    This represents the bus number and can be checked from the display and processor datasheets.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>I2C1_Read();</code> or <code>I2C2_Read();</code> or <code>I2C3_Read();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Byte from the I2C Bus in the lower 8 bits</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-137-1" name="__codelineno-137-1" href="#__codelineno-137-1"></a><span class="nl">c</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">I2C1_Read</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Read a single byte from the I2C1 Bus</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="i2cx_write">I2Cx_Write</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends a single byte to the I2C bus</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This functions is available for all 3 I2C buses of PIXXI-44 and 2 I2C buses of PIXXI-28.
The functions are prepended with <code>I2Cx</code> where x is 1 to 3.
This represents the bus number and can be checked from the display and processor datasheets.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>I2C1_Write(byte);</code> or <code>I2C2_Write(byte);</code> or <code>I2C3_Write(byte);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">byte</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The byte to be written to the I2C Bus</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>0</strong>: Failed</li>
<li><strong>1</strong>: Success</li>
<li><strong>2</strong>: NAK was received from device</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-138-1" name="__codelineno-138-1" href="#__codelineno-138-1"></a><span class="nl">status</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">I2C1_Write</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">bytevalue</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Send a single byte to the I2C</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="i2cx_ack">I2Cx_Ack</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends an I2C acknowledge condition. 
The hardware first pulls the SDA line low, and next releases SCL high followed by pulling SCL low again thus generating a clock pulse, SDA is then released high.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>Data can only change when the clock is low</li>
<li>This functions is available for all 3 I2C buses of PIXXI-44 and 2 I2C buses of PIXXI-28.
    The functions are prepended with <code>I2Cx</code> where x is 1 to 3.
    This represents the bus number and can be checked from the display and processor datasheets.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>I2C1_Ack();</code> or <code>I2C2_Ack();</code> or <code>I2C3_Ack();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-139-1" name="__codelineno-139-1" href="#__codelineno-139-1"></a><span class="n">I2C1_Ack</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Send I2C Acknowledge condition</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="i2cx_nack">I2Cx_Nack</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends an I2C negative acknowledge condition. 
The hardware first releases the SDA line high, and next releases SCL HI followed by pulling SCL low thus generating a clock pulse.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>Data can only change when the clock is low.</li>
<li>This functions is available for all 3 I2C buses of PIXXI-44 and 2 I2C buses of PIXXI-28.
    The functions are prepended with <code>I2Cx</code> where x is 1 to 3.
    This represents the bus number and can be checked from the display and processor datasheets.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>I2C1_Nack();</code> or <code>I2C2_Nack();</code> or <code>I2C3_Nack();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-140-1" name="__codelineno-140-1" href="#__codelineno-140-1"></a><span class="n">I2C1_Nack</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//Send an I2C Negative acknowledge condition</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="i2cx_ackstatus">I2Cx_AckStatus</h3>
<p>Call this function to get the ACK status from the slave device. 
The state of SDA is returned.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>Returns the state of SDA after the last clock pulse</li>
<li>This functions is available for all 3 I2C buses of PIXXI-44 and 2 I2C buses of PIXXI-28.
    The functions are prepended with <code>I2Cx</code> where x is 1 to 3.
    This represents the bus number and can be checked from the display and processor datasheets.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>I2C1_AckStatus();</code> or <code>I2C2_AckStatus();</code> or <code>I2C3_AckStatus();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Device ACK status</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-141-1" name="__codelineno-141-1" href="#__codelineno-141-1"></a><span class="nl">r</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">I2C1_AckStatus</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// returns the ACK Status</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 id="img_setposition">img_SetPosition</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a>.</p>
<p>Sets the position where the image will next be displayed. You may turn off an image using <a href="#img_disable">img_Disable()</a> so when <a href="#img_show">img_Show()</a> is called, the image will not be shown. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>img_SetPosition(handle, index, xpos, ypos);</code></p>

</tr>

</tr>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_setword">img_SetWord</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a>.</p>
<p>This set the specified word in an image entry. The following are the available parameters that can be set:</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>

<tr>

<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">IMAGE_YPOS</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the image location Y</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;"><p id="img_set_flags">IMAGE_FLAGS</p></td>
<td style="text-align: center;">6</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the image flags</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td style="text-align: center;">7</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the inter frame delay</td>
</tr>

<td style="text-align: center;">12</td>

<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">IMAGE_TAG2</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">13</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the user variable #2</td>
</tr>

<div class="admonition note">

Also, if frame is set to -1, just a rectangle will be drawn in background colour to blank an image.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_setattributes">img_SetAttributes</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a>.</p>
<p>This function sets one or more bits in the <a href="#img_set_flags">IMAGE_FLAGS</a> field of an image control entry.</p>
<p>A '1' bit in the "value" field sets the respective bit in the IMAGE_FLAGS field of the image control entry which may be combined with the + or | operators.</p>
<p class="small-padding-table"></p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Flag Constant</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Bit</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_ENABLED</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">15</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x8000</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">set for image enabled</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_DARKEN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">14</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x4000</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">display dimmed</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_LIGHTEN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">13</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x2000</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">display bright</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_TOUCHED</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">12</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x1000</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">touch test result</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_Y_LOCK</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">11</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0800</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">stop Y movement</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_X_LOCK</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">10</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0400</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">stop X movement</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_TOPMOST</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">9</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0200</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">draw on top of other images next update</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_STAYONTOP</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">8</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0100</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">draw on top of other images always</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">I_TOUCH_DISABLE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">5</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x0020</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">set to disable touch for this image:<br> <strong>1</strong> for movie or <strong>0</strong> for image</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<div class="admonition note">

<p>If index is set to -1, the attribute is altered in ALL the entries in the image list.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: True if successful</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-157-2" name="__codelineno-157-2" href="#__codelineno-157-2"></a><span class="n">img_ClearAttributes</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">ALL</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">I_Y_LOCK</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">|</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">I_X_LOCK</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="c1">// Allows movement in all images</span>

<h3 id="img_touched">img_Touched</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a>.</p>
<p>Returns index if image touched or returns -1 if no image was touched. </p>
<p>If index is passed as -1 the function tests all images and returns -1 if no image was touched or returns index.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>img_Touched(handle, index);</code></p>

</tr>
<tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the images in the list</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: <strong>index</strong> of image touched, released or being held, or <strong>-1</strong> if none</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_fileread">img_FileRead</h3>
<p>This requires that an image file control has been created with <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl</a> under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Reads the number of bytes specified by <strong>size</strong> from the file referenced by <strong>handle</strong> into a destination memory buffer. If <strong>dest</strong> is zero, data is directed to GRAM window.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>This is only available for use on the Flash based PmmC version.</li>
<li>This is only for files embedded in a GCF, for Flash only, ie. this is not valid for GCI and uSD card access.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>img_FileRead(*dest, size, handle, index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to a destination memory buffer</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of bytes to read</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Number of characters read</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-159-1" name="__codelineno-159-1" href="#__codelineno-159-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">img_FileRead</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">memblock</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hnd1</span><span class="p">);</span>
