<h3 class="page-break" id="img_fileseek">img_FileSeek</h3>
<p>This requires that an image file control has been created with <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl</a> under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Set file position to specified address for the file handle so subsequent data may be read from that position onwards with
<a href="#img_filegetc">img_FileGetC(...)</a>, <a href="#img_filegetw">img_FileGetW(...)</a> or <a href="#img_filegets">img_FileGetS(...)</a>.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>This is only available for use on the Flash based PmmC version.</li>
<li>This is only for files embedded in a GCF, for Flash only, ie. this is not valid for GCI and uSD card access.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>img_FileSeek(handle, index, HiWord, LoWord);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">HiWord</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the upper 16 bits of the file position</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LoWord</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the lower 16 bits of the file position</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: True if successful</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-160-1" name="__codelineno-160-1" href="#__codelineno-160-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">img_FileSeek</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x1234</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Set file position to 0x00001234 (byte position 4660)</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_filegets">img_FileGetS</h3>
<p>This requires that an image file control has been created with <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl</a> under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>This function reads a line of text to a buffer (specified by <strong>*string</strong>) from a file at the current file position indicated by the associated file-position pointer and advances the pointer appropriately. </p>
<p>This function reads only reads up to <strong>size - 1</strong> characters into <strong>*string</strong> (one character is reserved for the null-terminator).
Characters are read until either a newline or an EOF is received or until the number of characters read reaches <strong>size - 1</strong> or a read error is received.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>This is only available for use on the Flash based PmmC version.</li>
<li>This is only for files embedded in a GCF, for Flash only, ie. this is not valid for GCI and uSD card access.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>img_FileGetS(*string, size, handle, index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">string</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination buffer</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The maximum number of bytes to be read from the file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Returns pointer to string or NULL if failed</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_fileloadfunction">img_FileLoadFunction</h3>
<p>This requires that an image file control has been created with <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl</a> under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Load a function or program from disk and return a function pointer to the allocation.</p>
<p>The function can then be invoked just like any other function would be called via a function pointer.
Parameters may be passed to it in a conventional way. The caller's stack is shared by the loaded function, however any global variables in the loaded function are private to that function.</p>
<p>The function may be discarded at any time when no longer required, freeing its memory resources through <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(...)</a></p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>This is only available for use on the Flash based PmmC version.</li>
<li>This is only for files embedded in a GCF, for Flash only, ie. this is not valid for GCI and uSD card access.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>img_FileLoadFunction(handle, index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: pointer to the memory allocation where the function has been loaded from file which can be then used as a function call</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_filerun">img_FileRun</h3>
<p>This requires that an image file control has been created with <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl</a> under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Load a program from disk where the current program releases any allocated memory but retains the stack and global memory.</p>
<p>If arglistptr is 0, no arguments are passed, else, arglist points to an array, the first element being the number of elements in the array.</p>
<p>The func <strong>main</strong> in the called program accepts the arguments, if any. The arguments can only be passed by value, no pointers or references can be used as all memory is cleared before the file is loaded. </p>
<p>Refer to <a href="#img_fileexec">img_FileExec(...)</a> and <a href="#img_fileloadfunction">img_FileLoadFunction(...)</a> for functions that can pass by reference.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>This is only available for use on the Flash based PmmC version.</li>
<li>This is only for files embedded in a GCF, for Flash only, ie. this is not valid for GCI and uSD card access.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>img_FileRun(handle, index, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: the returned value from main in the called program</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-171-1" name="__codelineno-171-1" href="#__codelineno-171-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">img_FileRun</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">index</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">argptr</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="img_fileexec">img_FileExec</h3>
<p>This requires that an image file control has been created with <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl</a> under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Load a program from disk and returns like a function, the calling program is kept active, and control returns to it.</p>
<p>The function <strong>main</strong> in the called program accepts the arguments, if any. If <strong>arglistptr</strong> is 0, no arguments are passed, else <strong>arglist</strong> points to an array, the first element being the number of elements in the array. </p>
<p>This function is similar to <a href="#img_fileloadfunction">img_FileLoadFunction(...)</a>, however, the function argument list is passed by pointer, and the memory consumed by the function is released as soon as the function completes.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>This is only available for use on the Flash based PmmC version.</li>
<li>This is only for files embedded in a GCF, for Flash only, ie. this is not valid for GCI and uSD card access.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>img_FileExec(handle, index, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: the returned value from main in the called program</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-172-1" name="__codelineno-172-1" href="#__codelineno-172-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">img_FileExec</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">index</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">argptr</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_fileplaywav">img_FilePlayWAV</h3>
<p>This requires that an image file control has been created with <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl</a> under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Play a wave file at <strong>index</strong> in the image filesystem <strong>handle</strong>. This automatically grabs a chunk of memory for a file buffer, and a wave buffer. </p>
<p>The minimum memory requirement is about 580 bytes for disk I/O service and a minimum wave buffer size of 1024.
The size of wave buffer allocation can be increased by <a href="#snd_bufsize">snd_BufSize</a> function. The default size 1024 bytes.
The memory is only required during the duration of play and is automatically released while not in use.</p>
<p>See <a href="#sound-control-functions">Sound Control Functions</a> for additional play control functions.</p>
<p id="img_fileplayway_errors">This function may return the following error values:</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-7</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Insufficient memory available for WAV buffer and file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-6</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">cant play this rate</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-5</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no data chunk found in first rsector</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no format data</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no wave chunk signature</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">bad wave file format</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">file not found</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>This is only available for use on the Flash based PmmC version.</li>
<li>This is only for files embedded in a GCF, for Flash only, ie. this is not valid for GCI and uSD card access.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>img_FilePlayWAV(handle, index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Number of blocks to play (1 to 32767) or negative value in case of <a href="#img_fileplayway_errors">errors</a></p>
<p class="page-break"></p>

<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-173-1" name="__codelineno-173-1" href="#__codelineno-173-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">ding.wav</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_filecheckupdate">img_FileCheckUpdate</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image file control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a> under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Checks and/or updates the program running in Flash using the specified file in Flash memory.</p>
<p id="img_filecheckupdate_options">The following options determine the mode of operation:</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Option</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_QUERY</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Checks the specified file and compares its DateTime to the program running in Flash</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_UPDATENEWER</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Updates the program in Flash if the program on uSD is newer</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_UPDATEALWAYS</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Always updates the program in Flash</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p id="img_filecheckupdate_results">
If update occurs and the program is running from Flash, the display is reset after update.
Otherwise, if a query or an error occurs, the following is returned:
</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Option</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_NEWFILE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The specified file is newer than the file running in Flash</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_OLDFILE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The specified file is equal to or older than the file running in Flash</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_UPDATEDONE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">An update was performed, and the program is running from RAM</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_NOFILE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The specified file does not exist</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_functioncall">img_FunctionCall</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image file control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a> under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>This function loads and calls the Function found at index in the Flash GCI filesystem identified by handle.</p>
<p>Parameters <strong>state</strong>, <strong>&amp;FunctionRam</strong> and <strong>&amp;FunctionDef</strong> are passed. The first two parameters are passed "as is", since the third parameter is normally in flash, and one programs flash is not accessible from another.</p>
<p>The <strong>FunctionArgCount</strong> constant is copied into a RAM array and passed to the Function.</p>
<p>The parameter <strong>FunctionStringMap</strong> is a bit array of the indexes containing single and multiple stringsthat are offset by 8. e.g., 0x0100 means parameter 8 is a single string, 0x0002 means parameter 9 is an array of strings with parameter 8 containing the count.</p>
<p>Any function called this way is loaded into RAM and then left there. RAM is managed using a Least Recently Used (LRU) mechanism wherein the least recently used entry is freed if there is not enough Heap to load the desired function.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>This is only available for use on the Flash based PmmC version.</li>
<li>This is only for files embedded in a GCF, for Flash only, ie. this is not valid for GCI and uSD card access.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>img_FunctionCall(handle, index, state, &amp;FunctionRam, &amp;FunctionDef, FunctionArgCount, FunctionArgStringMap);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">state</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Value passed to update function state</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">FunctionRam</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the function RAM allocation</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">FunctionDef</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the function definitions stored in Flash</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">FunctionArgCount</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Function argument count</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">FunctionArgStringMap</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">String address array</td>
</tr>
</tbody>

<h3 class="page-break" id="intflash_functioncall">intflash_FunctionCall</h3>
<p>This function loads and calls the Function found at <strong>index</strong> in Internal Flash</p>
<p>Parameters <code>state</code>, <code>&amp;FncRam</code>, <code>&amp;FncDef</code> are passed.
The first two parameters are passed "as is", since the third parameter is normally in flash, and one programs flash is not accessible from another.</p>
<p>The <strong>FncArgCount</strong> constant is copied into a RAM array and passed to the Function.</p>
<p>The parameter <strong>FncArgStrMap</strong> is a bit array of the indexes containing single and multiple strings that are offset by 8. e.g. 0x0100 means parameter 8 is a single string, 0x0002 means parameter 9 is an array of strings with parameter 8 containing the count.</p>
<p>Any function called this way is loaded into RAM and then left there. RAM is managed using a Least Recently Used (LRU) mechanism wherein the least recently used entry is freed if there is not enough Heap to load the desired function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>intflash_FunctionCall(handle, index, state, &amp;FncRam, &amp;FncDef, FncArgCount, FncArgStrMap);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">state</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Value passed to update function state</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;FncRam</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the function RAM allocation</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;FncDef</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the function definitions stored in Flash</td>

<td style="text-align: left;">Function argument count</td>

<td style="text-align: left;">String address array</td>
</tr>

<h3 id="rand">RAND</h3>
<p>This function returns a pseudo random signed number ranging from -32768 to +32767.</p>
<p>Returns a pseudo random signed number ranging from -32768 to +32767 each time the function is called. The random number generator may first be seeded by using the SEED(number) function. The seed will generate a pseudo random sequence that is repeatable. You can use the modulo operator (%) to return a number within a certain range, eg n := RAND() % 100; will return a random number between -99 and +99. If you are using random number generation for random graphics points, or only require a positive number set, you will need to use the ABS function so only a positive number is returned, eg: X1 := ABS(RAND() % 100); will set co-ordinate X1 between 0 and 99. Note that if the random number generator is not seeded, the first number returned after reset or power up will be zero. This is normal behavior. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>RAND();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: pseudo random signed number ranging from -32768 to +32767.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-190-1" name="__codelineno-190-1" href="#__codelineno-190-1"></a><span class="n">SEED</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1234</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-190-2" name="__codelineno-190-2" href="#__codelineno-190-2"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print '3558, 1960' to the display.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-190-3" name="__codelineno-190-3" href="#__codelineno-190-3"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">(),</span><span class="s">", "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">());</span>
</code></pre></div>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>SEED(number);</code></p>

</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-191-2" name="__codelineno-191-2" href="#__codelineno-191-2"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print '30129, 27266' to the display.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-191-3" name="__codelineno-191-3" href="#__codelineno-191-3"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">(),</span><span class="s">", "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">());</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="sqrt">SQRT</h3>
<p>This function returns the <strong>integer square root</strong> which is the greatest integer less than or equal to the square root of <strong>number</strong>. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>SQRT(number);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>

</thead>

<tr>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: the <strong>integer square root</strong> of a number.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-192-1" name="__codelineno-192-1" href="#__codelineno-192-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-192-2" name="__codelineno-192-2" href="#__codelineno-192-2"></a><span class="c1">// returns 161 in 'myvar' which is the 'integer square root' of 26000</span>
<a id="__codelineno-192-3" name="__codelineno-192-3" href="#__codelineno-192-3"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">SQRT</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">26000</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="ovf">OVF</h3>
<p>This function returns the high order 16 bits from certain math and shift functions. It is extremely useful for calculating 32 bit address offsets for MEDIA access. It can be used with the shift operations, addition, subtraction, multiplication and modulus operations.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>OVF();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: the high order 16 bits from certain math and shift functions.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-193-1" name="__codelineno-193-1" href="#__codelineno-193-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">loWord</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hiWord</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-193-2" name="__codelineno-193-2" href="#__codelineno-193-2"></a><span class="nl">loWord</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x2710</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">*</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x2710</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// (10000 * 10000 in hex format)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-193-3" name="__codelineno-193-3" href="#__codelineno-193-3"></a><span class="nl">hiWord</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OVF</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-193-4" name="__codelineno-193-4" href="#__codelineno-193-4"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"0x"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">HEX</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hiWord</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">HEX</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">loWord</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-193-5" name="__codelineno-193-5" href="#__codelineno-193-5"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print '0x05F5E100' to the display</span>
<a id="__codelineno-193-6" name="__codelineno-193-6" href="#__codelineno-193-6"></a><span class="c1">// which is 100,000,000 in hexadecimal</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="cy">CY</h3>
<p>This function returns the carry status of an unsigned overflow from any 16 or 32bit additions or subtractions.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>CY();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: 0 or 1 as the status of carry.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-194-1" name="__codelineno-194-1" href="#__codelineno-194-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-194-2" name="__codelineno-194-2" href="#__codelineno-194-2"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xFFF8</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">+</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">9</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">                                </span><span class="c1">// result = 1</span>
<a id="__codelineno-194-3" name="__codelineno-194-3" href="#__codelineno-194-3"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"myvar "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">Carry "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">CY</span><span class="p">(),</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="c1">// carry = 1</span>
<a id="__codelineno-194-4" name="__codelineno-194-4" href="#__codelineno-194-4"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-194-5" name="__codelineno-194-5" href="#__codelineno-194-5"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print 'myvar 1 Carry 1'</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="umul_1616">umul_1616</h3>

<h3 id="ucmp_3232">ucmp_3232</h3>
<p>This function performs an unsigned comparison of 2 x 32bit values. The result of the subtraction is returned.</p>
<p>This function does not affect the carry flag.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>ucmp_3232(&amp;val1, &amp;val2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;val1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">points to 32bit augend</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;val2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">points to 32bit addend</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: </p>
<ul>
<li><strong>0</strong> if val1 = val2 </li>
<li><strong>1</strong> if val1 &gt; val2 </li>
<li><strong>-1</strong> if val1 &lt; val2</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-198-1" name="__codelineno-198-1" href="#__codelineno-198-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">valA</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">valB</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Result</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-198-2" name="__codelineno-198-2" href="#__codelineno-198-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-198-3" name="__codelineno-198-3" href="#__codelineno-198-3"></a><span class="n">valA</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-198-4" name="__codelineno-198-4" href="#__codelineno-198-4"></a><span class="n">valA</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xFFFF</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-198-5" name="__codelineno-198-5" href="#__codelineno-198-5"></a><span class="n">valB</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-198-6" name="__codelineno-198-6" href="#__codelineno-198-6"></a><span class="n">valB</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0xEFFF</span><span class="p">;</span>

<h3 id="udiv_3232">udiv_3232</h3>
<p>This function performs an unsigned division of 2 x 32bit values placing the 32bit result in a 2 word array.
<strong>Note</strong> A division by zero will result is <em>0xFFFFFFFF</em>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>udiv_3232(&amp;res32, val1, val2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;res32</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to 32bit result register.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">val1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">32bit register or dividend.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">val2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">32bit register or divisor.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: the pointer to the 32bit result. Carry and overflow are not affected. </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-199-1" name="__codelineno-199-1" href="#__codelineno-199-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">val32</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">dividend</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">divisor</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-199-2" name="__codelineno-199-2" href="#__codelineno-199-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">p</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-199-3" name="__codelineno-199-3" href="#__codelineno-199-3"></a><span class="n">dividend</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x5c21</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="c1">// part of 1661985</span>
<a id="__codelineno-199-4" name="__codelineno-199-4" href="#__codelineno-199-4"></a><span class="n">dividend</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x19</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="c1">// part of 1661985</span>
<a id="__codelineno-199-5" name="__codelineno-199-5" href="#__codelineno-199-5"></a><span class="n">divisor</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">13</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-199-6" name="__codelineno-199-6" href="#__codelineno-199-6"></a><span class="n">divisor</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">1</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>

<h2 class="page-break" id="media-functions">Media Functions</h2>
<p>The media can be SD/SDHC, microSD or serial (NAND) flash device interfaced to the SPI port.</p>
<h3 id="media_init">media_Init</h3>
<p>Initialise a uSD/SD/SDHC memory card or a SPI Flash memory device (&lt; 32 MB) for further operations. 
The SD card or Flash device is connected to the SPI (serial peripheral interface) of the processor.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>media_Init();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>1</strong> if uSD is found, and has been successfully initialised</li>
<li><strong>0</strong> if uSD is not present, or SPI memory is present</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-200-1" name="__codelineno-200-1" href="#__codelineno-200-1"></a><span class="c1">// Waits for SD card to be inserted and initialised, flashing a message if no SD card detected.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-200-2" name="__codelineno-200-2" href="#__codelineno-200-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-200-3" name="__codelineno-200-3" href="#__codelineno-200-3"></a><span class="k">while</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="n">media_Init</span><span class="p">())</span>
<a id="__codelineno-200-4" name="__codelineno-200-4" href="#__codelineno-200-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">gfx_Cls</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-200-5" name="__codelineno-200-5" href="#__codelineno-200-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">300</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-200-6" name="__codelineno-200-6" href="#__codelineno-200-6"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">puts</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Please insert SD card"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-200-7" name="__codelineno-200-7" href="#__codelineno-200-7"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">300</span><span class="p">);</span>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="media_init4">media_Init4</h3>
<p>The command used to set the flash memory into 4 byte addressing mode, This is not used with uSD cards, only for SPI flash memory that requires 4 byte addressing (ie cards &gt; 32MB).
The SPI Flash device is connected to the SPI (serial peripheral interface) of the processor.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>media_Init4(command);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">FLASH_ADDR_DEF_COMMAND</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The default command will be used to switch most chips into 4 byte mode (0xB7).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">FLASH_ADDR_ALWAYS_4BYTE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">No command will be sent (for chips permanently in 4 byte mode)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">0x??</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">For chips that don't use 0xB7 to put them into 4 byte mode. Refer to the Datasheet associated with the Flash Memory in question.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>1</strong> if uSD is found (Error, this command should not be used when a uSD card is present) </li>
<li><strong>0</strong> if uSD is not present (good) and therefore SPI memory card is present and successfully initialised</li>
</ul>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>For systems with SPI Flash memory device the response will be 0, however, this function still needs to be called to initialise the Flash memory chip.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-201-1" name="__codelineno-201-1" href="#__codelineno-201-1"></a><span class="c1">// This example simply initialises the SPI Flash memory into 4 byte mode for a 32MB card</span>
<a id="__codelineno-201-2" name="__codelineno-201-2" href="#__codelineno-201-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-201-3" name="__codelineno-201-3" href="#__codelineno-201-3"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="n">media_Init4</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">FLASH_ADDR_DEF_COMMAND</span><span class="p">))</span>
<a id="__codelineno-201-4" name="__codelineno-201-4" href="#__codelineno-201-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">puts</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Flash memory initialised"</span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-201-5" name="__codelineno-201-5" href="#__codelineno-201-5"></a><span class="n">Endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="media_initspeed">media_InitSpeed</h3>
<p>Initialise a uSD/SD/SDHC memory card at a given speed. The SD card is connected to the SPI (Serial Peripheral Interface) of the processor. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>media_InitSpeed(speed);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">speed</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the speed. Speed can be from <strong>SPI_SPEED0</strong> (slowest) to <strong>SPI_SPEED15</strong> (fastest).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: 1 if memory card is successfully initialised, otherwise returns 0</p>

<h3 id="media_setadd">media_SetAdd</h3>
<p>Set media memory internal Address pointer for access at a non sector aligned byte address. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>media_SetAdd(HIword, LOword);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">HIword</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the high word (upper 2 bytes) of a 4 byte media memory byte address location.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LOword</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the low word (lower 2 bytes) of a 4 byte media memory byte address location.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

</tr>
</thead>

<td style="text-align: left;">Destination block pointed to by the internal Sector pointer.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li>TRUE if media response was TRUE.</li>
<li>512 bytes (256 words) in to a destination block.</li>
</ul>

<h3 id="media_writebyte">media_WriteByte</h3>

</thead>

<a id="__codelineno-209-7" name="__codelineno-209-7" href="#__codelineno-209-7"></a><span class="w">                                    </span><span class="c1">// lower 9 bits</span>

<a id="__codelineno-209-11" name="__codelineno-209-11" href="#__codelineno-209-11"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-209-12" name="__codelineno-209-12" href="#__codelineno-209-12"></a><span class="nf">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">MDA</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Hello World"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="c1">// now write a ascii test string</span>

<a id="__codelineno-209-14" name="__codelineno-209-14" href="#__codelineno-209-14"></a><span class="n">media_WriteByte</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sc">'B'</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-209-15" name="__codelineno-209-15" href="#__codelineno-209-15"></a><span class="n">media_WriteByte</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sc">'C'</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-209-16" name="__codelineno-209-16" href="#__codelineno-209-16"></a><span class="n">media_WriteByte</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                 </span><span class="c1">// terminate with zero</span>
<a id="__codelineno-209-17" name="__codelineno-209-17" href="#__codelineno-209-17"></a><span class="n">media_Flush</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">                      </span><span class="c1">// we're finished, close the sector</span>
<a id="__codelineno-209-18" name="__codelineno-209-18" href="#__codelineno-209-18"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-209-19" name="__codelineno-209-19" href="#__codelineno-209-19"></a><span class="n">media_SetAdd</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1024</span><span class="o">+</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">            </span><span class="c1">// set the starting byte address</span>
<a id="__codelineno-209-20" name="__codelineno-209-20" href="#__codelineno-209-20"></a><span class="k">while</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="n">media_ReadByte</span><span class="p">())</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">putch</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// print result, starting</span>
<a id="__codelineno-209-21" name="__codelineno-209-21" href="#__codelineno-209-21"></a><span class="w">                                            </span><span class="c1">// from '5'</span>
<a id="__codelineno-209-22" name="__codelineno-209-22" href="#__codelineno-209-22"></a><span class="n">repeat</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">forever</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Due to design constraints on the PIXXI, there is no way of writing bytes or words within a media sector without starting from the beginning of the sector. All writes will start at the beginning of a sector and are incremental until the <a href="#media_flush"><strong>media_Flush()</strong></a> function is executed, or the sector address rolls over to the next sector. Any remaining bytes in the sector will be padded with <strong>0xFF</strong>, destroying the previous contents. An attempt to use the <a href="#media_setadd"><strong>media_SetAdd(..)</strong></a> function will result in the lower 9 bits being interpreted as zero. If the writing rolls over to the next sector, the media_Flush() function is issued automatically internally.</p>
</div>

<h3 id="media_flush">media_Flush</h3>
<p>After writing any data to a sector, media_Flush() should be called to ensure that the current sector that is being written is correctly stored back to the media else write operations may be unpredictable.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Flush();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<p>See the <a href="#media_writebyte">media_WriteByte(..)</a> and <a href="#media_writeword">media_WriteWord(..)</a> examples.</p>
<h3 id="media_image">media_Image</h3>
<p>Displays an image from the media storage at the specified co-ordinates. The image address is previously specified with the <a href="#media_setadd"><strong>media_SetAdd(..)</strong></a> or <a href="#media_setsector"><strong>media_SetSector(...)</strong></a> function. If the image is shown partially off screen, it is necessary to enable clipping for it to be displayed correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Image(x, y);</code></p>

</table></div></div>

<h3 id="media_video">media_Video</h3>
<p>Displays a <em>video</em> clip from the media storage device at the specified co-ordinates. The <em>video</em> address location in the media is previously specified with the <a href="#media_setadd"><strong>media_SetAdd(..)</strong></a> or <a href="#media_setsector"><strong>media_SetSector(...)</strong></a> function. If the <em>video</em> is shown partially off screen, it is necessary to enable clipping for it be displayed correctly. Note that showing a <em>video</em> blocks all other processes until the video has finished showing. See the <a href="#media_videoframe"><strong>media_VideoFrame(...)</strong></a> functions for alternatives.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>media_Video(x, y);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the top left position where the video clip will be displayed.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>

<h3 id="media_videoframe">media_VideoFrame</h3>
<p>Displays a <em>video</em> from the media storage device at the specified co-ordinates. The <em>video</em> address is previously specified with the <a href="#media_setadd"><strong>media_SetAdd(..)</strong></a> or <a href="#media_setsector"><strong>media_SetSector(...)</strong></a> function. If the <em>video</em> is shown partially off screen, it is necessary to enable clipping for it be displayed correctly. The frames can be shown in any order. This function gives you great flexibility for showing various icons from an image strip, as well as showing videos while doing other tasks</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>media_VideoFrame(x, y, frameNumber);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the top left position where the video clip will be displayed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">frameBuffer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the required frame to be shown.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>

<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>It is assumed that the media has been loaded with the example video in GFX2DEMO.GCI loaded at sector 0. This can be loaded using the Graphics Composer directly onto the memory card.</p>

<h2 id="memory-allocation-functions">Memory Allocation Functions</h2>
<h3 id="mem_alloc">mem_Alloc</h3>
<p>Allocate a block of memory to a pointer. The allocated memory contains garbage but is a fast allocation. The block must later be released with <a href="#mem_free"><strong>mem_Free(…)</strong></a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>mem_Alloc(size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes that's allocated from the heap.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: If successful, the return value is the pointer (Word) to the allocation, otherwise null (0). </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-215-1" name="__codelineno-215-1" href="#__codelineno-215-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Alloc</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_allocv">mem_AllocV</h3>
<p>Allocate a block of memory to a pointer. The block of memory is filled with initial signature values. The block starts with A5,5A then fills with incrementing number eg:- A5,5A,00,01,02,03...FF,00,11.... This can be helpful when debugging. The block must later be released with <a href="#mem_free"><strong>mem_Free(…)</strong></a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>mem_AllocV(size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes that's allocated from the heap.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: If successful, the return value is the pointer (Word) to the allocation, otherwise null (0). </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-216-1" name="__codelineno-216-1" href="#__codelineno-216-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_AllocV</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_allocz">mem_AllocZ</h3>
<p>Allocate a block of memory to pointer myvar. The block of memory is filled with zeros. 
The block must later be released with <a href="#mem_free"><strong>mem_Free(…)</strong></a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>mem_AllocZ(size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes that's allocated from the heap.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: If successful, the return value is the pointer (Word) to the allocation, otherwise null (0). </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-217-1" name="__codelineno-217-1" href="#__codelineno-217-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_AllocZ</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_realloc">mem_Realloc</h3>
<p>The function may move the memory block to a new location, in which case the pointer to the new location is returned. 
The content of the memory block is preserved up to the lesser of the new and old sizes, even if the block is moved. 
If the new size is larger, the value of the newly allocated portion is indeterminate. 
In case that ptr is NULL, the function behaves exactly as <a href="#mem_alloc">mem_Alloc(…)</a>, assigning a new block of size bytes and returning a pointer to the beginning of it. 
In case that the size is 0, the memory previously allocated in ptr is deallocated as if a call to <a href="#mem_free"><strong>mem_Free(…)</strong></a> was made, and a NULL pointer is returned.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>mem_Realloc(ptr, size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the new location to reallocate the memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes of the block.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: Pointer to the new object location </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-218-1" name="__codelineno-218-1" href="#__codelineno-218-1"></a><span class="nl">newptr</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Realloc</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myptr</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_free">mem_Free</h3>
<p>The function de-allocates a block of memory previously created with <a href="#mem_alloc">mem_Alloc(...)</a>, <a href="#mem_allocv">mem_AllocV(...)</a> or <a href="#mem_allocz">mem_AllocZ(...)</a>. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>mem_Free(allocation);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">allocation</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the location of memory block to free up.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: non-zero if function is successful, otherwise 0 if it fails </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-219-1" name="__codelineno-219-1" href="#__codelineno-219-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Free</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">buffer</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_heap">mem_Heap</h3>
<p>Returns byte size of the largest chunk of memory available in the heap. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>mem_Heap();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: the largest available memory chunk of the heap. </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-220-1" name="__codelineno-220-1" href="#__codelineno-220-1"></a><span class="nl">howmuch</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Heap</span><span class="p">();</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_set">mem_Set</h3>
<p>Fill a block of memory with a byte value.  </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>mem_Set(ptr, char, size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the value to fill the block with.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the size of the block in Bytes.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: the pointer </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-221-1" name="__codelineno-221-1" href="#__codelineno-221-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mybuf</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">];</span>

<a id="__codelineno-221-5" name="__codelineno-221-5" href="#__codelineno-221-5"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-221-6" name="__codelineno-221-6" href="#__codelineno-221-6"></a><span class="n">mem_Set</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mh">0x55</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//Only fills half of mybuf[]</span>
<a id="__codelineno-221-7" name="__codelineno-221-7" href="#__codelineno-221-7"></a><span class="k">for</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">i</span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="n">i</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="k">sizeof</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="n">i</span><span class="o">++</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">//Show what is in the buffer</span>

<h3 id="mem_compare">mem_Compare</h3>
<p>Compare two blocks of memory <strong>ptr1</strong> and <strong>ptr2</strong>. The comparison is done alphabetically. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>mem_Compare(ptr1, ptr2, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the 1st memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the 2nd memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes to compare.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li>0 if we have a match</li>
<li>-1 if ptr1 &lt; ptr2</li>
<li>+1 if ptr2 &gt; ptr1</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-223-1" name="__codelineno-223-1" href="#__codelineno-223-1"></a><span class="nl">test</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Compare</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">this_block</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">that_block</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 class="page-break" id="miscellaneous-system-functions">Miscellaneous System Functions</h2>
<h3 id="sys_pmmc">sys_PmmC</h3>
<p>Prints the system PmmC name and revision, e.g. "PIXXI\n1.0". Can be captured to a buffer using the <a href="#to">to()</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>sys_PmmC();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: PmmC version</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-224-1" name="__codelineno-224-1" href="#__codelineno-224-1"></a><span class="n">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myString</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">sys_PmmC</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="c1">// save PmmC name and revision to buffer</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="sys_driver">sys_Driver</h3>
<p>Prints the system driver name and date string, eg " pixxiLCD-XXXXX”. Can be captured to a buffer using the <a href="#to">to()</a> function. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>sys_Driver();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-225-1" name="__codelineno-225-1" href="#__codelineno-225-1"></a><span class="n">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mystring</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">sys_Driver</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="c1">// save Driver name to buffer</span>
</code></pre></div>

<p>Baud rates each have degree of accuracy for several reasons. The actual baud rate you would receive and relevant error% compared to the setting value, can be calculated. </p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-226-1" name="__codelineno-226-1" href="#__codelineno-226-1"></a>ActualBaud = 4375000/(trunc(4375000/RequiredBaud)) 
<a id="__codelineno-226-2" name="__codelineno-226-2" href="#__codelineno-226-2"></a>Example for 115200 is, 4375000/115200 = 37.977, Trucated is 37. 4375000/37 = 118243 (rounded). 
<a id="__codelineno-226-3" name="__codelineno-226-3" href="#__codelineno-226-3"></a>Error% therefore is % difference between 115200 and 118243, therefore 2.64%
</code></pre></div>
<p>It is desirable to only use a baud rate between 2 devices which has a difference of typically &lt; 2%. Note both devices will have a degree of error, not just this 4D Processor, both need to be considered. </p>
</div>

<h3 id="com_setbaud">com_SetBaud</h3>
<p>Use this function to set the required baud rate for the required Com port, COM0 or COM1. Sets to any viable baud rate from 160 to 655350.</p>
<p>The default Baud Rate for COM0 is 115,200 bits per second or 115,200 baud. </p>
<p>There is no default Baud Rate for COM1, setting the baud rate also activates the pins for RX and TX.  Note: COM1 only exists on Pixxi-44 in Mode 2 (4-Wire SPI). </p>

<h3 id="serin">serin</h3>
<p>Receives a character from the Serial Port COM0. The transmission format is:
<strong>No Parity, 1 Stop Bit, 8 Data Bits</strong> (N,8,1).
The default Baud Rate is 115,200 bits per second or 115,200 baud. The baud rate can be changed under program control by using the <a href="#setbaud"><strong>setbaud(...)</strong></a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>serin();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>-1</strong> if no character is available</li>
<li><strong>-2</strong> if a framing error or over-run has occurred (auto cleared)</li>
<li><strong>0 or a positive value</strong> (up to 255) for a valid character received </li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-231-1" name="__codelineno-231-1" href="#__codelineno-231-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-231-2" name="__codelineno-231-2" href="#__codelineno-231-2"></a><span class="nl">char</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">serin</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">            </span><span class="c1">// test the com port</span>
<a id="__codelineno-231-3" name="__codelineno-231-3" href="#__codelineno-231-3"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&gt;=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">              </span><span class="c1">// if a valid character is received</span>
<a id="__codelineno-231-4" name="__codelineno-231-4" href="#__codelineno-231-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">process</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">          </span><span class="c1">// process the character</span>
<a id="__codelineno-231-5" name="__codelineno-231-5" href="#__codelineno-231-5"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_init">com_Init</h3>
<p>This is the initialisation function for the serial communications buffered service. Once initialised, the service runs in the background capturing and buffering serial data without the user application having to constantly poll the serial port. This frees up the application to service other tasks. </p>
<p><strong>MODES OF OPERATION</strong></p>
<dl>
<dt><strong>No qualifier – simple ring buffer (aka circular queue)</strong></dt>
<dd>
<p>If the <strong>qualifier</strong> is set to zero, the <strong>buffer</strong> is continually active as a simple circular queue. Characters when received from the host are placed in the circular queue (at the 'head' of the queue) Bytes may be removed from the circular queue (from the 'tail' of the queue) using the <a href="#serin"><strong>serin()</strong></a> function. If the tail is the same position as the head, there are no bytes in the queue, therefore <a href="#serin"><strong>serin()</strong></a> will return <strong>-1</strong>, meaning no character is available, also, the <a href="#com_count"><strong>com_Count()</strong></a> function can be read at any time to determine the number of characters that are waiting between the tail and head of the queue. If the queue is not read frequently by the application, and characters are still being sent by the host, the head will eventually catch up with the tail setting the internal COM_FULL flag (which can be read with the <a href="#com_full"><strong>com_Full()</strong></a> function) . Any further characters from the host are are now discarded, however, all the characters that were buffered up to this point are readable. This is a good way of reading a fixed size packet and not necessarily considered to be an error condition. If no characters are removed from the buffer until the COM_FULL flag (which can be read with the <a href="#com_full"><strong>com_Full()</strong></a> function) becomes set, it is guaranteed that the bytes will be ordered in the <strong>buffer</strong> from the start position, therefore, the <strong>buffer</strong> can be treated as an array and can be read directly without using <a href="#serin"><strong>serin()</strong></a> at all. In the latter case, the correct action is to process the data from the buffer, re-initialise the buffer with the <a href="#com_init"><strong>com_Init(..)</strong></a> function, or reset the buffered serial service by issuing the <a href="#com_reset"><strong>com_Reset()</strong></a> function (which will return serial reception to polled mode) , and send an acknowledgement to the host (traditionally a <strong>ACK</strong> or 6) to indicate that the application is ready to receive more data and the previous 'packet' has been dealt with, or conversely, the application may send a negative acknowledgement to indicate that some sort of error occurred, or the action could not be completed (traditionally a <strong>NAK</strong> or 16) .</p>
<p>If any low level errors occur during the buffering service (such as framing or over-run) the internal COM_ERROR flag will be set (which can be read with the <a href="#com_error"><strong>com_Error()</strong></a> function). </p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The COM_FULL flag will remain latched to indicate that the buffer did become full, and is not reset (even if all the characters are read) until the <a href="#com_init">com_Init(..)</a> or <a href="#com_reset">com_Reset()</a> function is issued.</p>
</div>
</dd>
<dt><strong>Using a qualifier</strong></dt>
<dd>
<p>If a <strong>qualifier</strong> character is specified, after the buffer is initialised with <a href="#com_init"><strong>com_Init(..)</strong></a> , the service will ignore all characters until the <strong>qualifier</strong> is received and only then initiate the buffer write sequence with incoming data. After that point, the behaviour is the same as above for the 'non qualified' mode.</p>
</dd>
</dl>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">buffer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the address of a buffer used for the background buffering service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">bufsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the byte size of the user array provided for the buffer (each array element holds 2 bytes). If the buffer size is zero, a buffer of 128 words (256 bytes) should be provided for automatic packet length mode (see below).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">qualifier</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the qualifying character that must be received to initiate serial data reception and buffer write. A zero (0x00) indicates no qualifier to be used.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-233-1" name="__codelineno-233-1" href="#__codelineno-233-1"></a><span class="n">com_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">combuf</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-233-2" name="__codelineno-233-2" href="#__codelineno-233-2"></a><span class="c1">// set up a comms ring buffer, maximum 12 characters before overflow</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_reset">com_Reset</h3>

<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>
