</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_count">com_Count</h3>
<p>This function can be read at any time (when in buffered communications is active) to determine the number of characters that are waiting in the buffer.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Count();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Current count of characters in the communications buffer.</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-235-1" name="__codelineno-235-1" href="#__codelineno-235-1"></a><span class="nl">n</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">com_Count</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// get the number of chars available in the buffer</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_full">com_Full</h3>
<p>If the queue is not read frequently by the application, and characters are still being sent by the host, the head will eventually catch up with the tail setting the <strong>COM_FULL</strong> flag which is read with this function. If this flag is set, any further characters from the host are discarded, however, all the characters that were buffered up to this point are readable.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Full();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  <strong>1</strong> if buffer or queue has become full, or is overflowed, else returns <strong>0</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-236-1" name="__codelineno-236-1" href="#__codelineno-236-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">com_Full</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">com_Count</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">==</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">))</span><span class="w"> </span>
<a id="__codelineno-236-2" name="__codelineno-236-2" href="#__codelineno-236-2"></a><span class="w">   </span><span class="n">com_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// buffer full, recovery</span>
<a id="__codelineno-236-3" name="__codelineno-236-3" href="#__codelineno-236-3"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_error">com_Error</h3>
<p>If any low level errors occur during the buffering service (such as framing or over-run) the internal <strong>COM_ERROR</strong> flag will be set which can be read with this function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Error();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: non-zero if any low level communications error occurred</p>
<ul>
<li>bit0 = Receiver Overflow Error</li>
<li>bit1 = Receiver Framing Error</li>
<li>bit2 = Parity Error Overflow</li>
<li>bit7 = Attempt to transmit when transmit is buffered and held</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-237-1" name="__codelineno-237-1" href="#__codelineno-237-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">com_Error</span><span class="p">())</span><span class="w">       </span><span class="c1">// if there were low level comms errors,</span>
<a id="__codelineno-237-2" name="__codelineno-237-2" href="#__codelineno-237-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">resetMySystem</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// take corrective action</span>
<a id="__codelineno-237-3" name="__codelineno-237-3" href="#__codelineno-237-3"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_sync">com_Sync</h3>
<p>If a <strong>qualifier</strong> character is specified when using buffered communications, after the buffer is initialized with <a href="#com_init">com_Init(..)</a> , the service will ignore all characters until the <strong>qualifier</strong> is received and only then initiate the buffer write sequence with incoming data. The <strong>com_Sync()</strong> function is called to determine if the qualifier character has been received yet.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Sync();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: <strong>1</strong> if the qualifier character has been received, else returns <strong>0</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-238-1" name="__codelineno-238-1" href="#__codelineno-238-1"></a><span class="n">com_Sync</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// reset to polled mode</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer</h3>
<p>Initialise a serial buffer for the COM0 or COM1 output. </p>
<p>The program must declare a var array as a circular buffer. When a TX buffer is declared for comms, the transmission of characters becomes non-blocking. The only time blocking will occur is if the buffer has insufficient space to accept the next character, in which case the function will wait for buffer space to become available. If the TX buffer is no longer required, just set the buffer pointer to zero, the size in this case doesn’t matter and is ignored. The function can resize or reallocated to another buffer at any time. The buffer is flushed before any changes are made.</p>
<p>"<strong>pin</strong>" designates an IO pin to control a bi-directional control device for half duplex mode. "<strong>pin</strong>" will go HI at the start of a transmission, and will return low after the final byte is transmitted. </p>
<p>Once the buffer has been initialised you just continue to use <a href="#serout">serout()</a> in the usual way, no other programming changes are required.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_TXbuffer(buf, bufsize, pin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the address of a buffer used for the buffering service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">bufsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the byte size of the user array provided for the buffer (each array element holds 2 bytes).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">pin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the turnaround pin. If not required, just set "pin" to zero.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-239-1" name="__codelineno-239-1" href="#__codelineno-239-1"></a><span class="n">com_TXbuffer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1024</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">IO1_PIN</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">       </span><span class="c1">// set the TX buffer</span>
<a id="__codelineno-239-2" name="__codelineno-239-2" href="#__codelineno-239-2"></a><span class="n">com_TXbuffer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">              </span><span class="c1">// revert to non buffered service</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_txbufferhold">com_TXbufferHold</h3>
<p>This function is used in conjunction with <a href="#com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer(...);</a>.
It is often necessary to hold off sending serial characters until a complete frame or packet has been built in the output buffer. <strong>com_TXbufferHold(ON)</strong> is used for this, to stop the buffer being sent while it is being loaded. Normally, when using buffered comms, the transmit process will begin immediately. This is fine unless you are trying to assemble a packet.</p>
<p>To build a packet and send it later, issue a <strong>com_TXbufferHold(ON);</strong>, build the packet, when packet is ready, issuing <strong>com_TXbufferHold(OFF);</strong>  will release the buffer to the com port. </p>
<p>Also, if using <a href="#com_txemptyevent">com_TXemptyEvent</a>, erroneous empty events will occur as the transmit buffer is constantly trying to empty while you are busy trying to fill it.</p>
<p>Also refer to the pin control for <a href="#com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer(...);</a> function. </p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>If you fill the buffer whilst it is held comms error 4 will be set and the data written will be lost.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_TXbufferHold(state);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">state</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the state of the buffer used for the buffering service.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li>Buffer count when called with argument of 1, for example <strong>com_TXbufferHold(ON)</strong></li>
<li>0 when argument is zero, eg <strong>com_TXbufferHold(OFF)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>
<p>Refer to the <a href="#com_txemptyevent">com_TXemptyEvent</a> example.</p>
<h3 id="com_txcount">com_TXcount</h3>
<p>Return count of characters remaining in COM0 or COM1 transmit buffer that was previously allocated with <a href="#com_txbuffer"><strong>com_TXbuffer(...)</strong></a> or <strong>com1_TXbuffer(...)</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_TXcount();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: count of characters</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-240-1" name="__codelineno-240-1" href="#__codelineno-240-1"></a><span class="nl">arg</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">com1_TXCount</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//return count of characters in COM1 TX buffer</span>

<h3 id="com_txemptyevent">com_TXemptyEvent</h3>
<p>If a comms TX buffer that was previously allocated with <a href="#com_txbuffer"><strong>com_TXbuffer(...);</strong></a> or <strong>com1_TXbuffer(...);</strong>, this function can be used to set up a function to be called when the COM0 or COM1 TX buffer is empty.
This is useful for either reloading the TX buffer, setting or clearing a pin to change the direction of eg a RS485 line driver, or any other form of traffic control. The event function must not have any parameters. To disable the event, simply call <strong>com_TXemptyEvent(0)</strong> or <strong>com1_TXemptyEvent(0)</strong>. <strong>com_TXbuffer(...);</strong> or <strong>com1_TXbuffer(...)</strong>; also resets any active event.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_TXemptyEvent(function);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">functionAddress</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Address of the event Function to be queued when COM TX buffer empty.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: any previous event function address, or zero if there was no previous function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>

<h3 id="com_initbrk">com_InitBrk</h3>
<p>This is the initialisation function for the serial communications buffered service with the ability to receive the BREAK signal as though it is a character. The parameters are identical to <a href="#com_init">com_Init()</a> except that each buffer entry can now only hold one byte. The BREAK ‘character’ is is a predefined constant call BREAK.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_InitBrk(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">buffer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the address of a buffer used for the background buffering service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">bufsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the byte size of the user array provided for the buffer (each array element holds 1 byte). If the buffer size is zero, a buffer of 128 words (256 bytes) should be provided for automatic packet length mode (see below).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">qualifier</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the qualifying character that must be received to initiate serial data reception and buffer write. A zero (0x00) indicates no qualifier to be used.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-242-1" name="__codelineno-242-1" href="#__codelineno-242-1"></a><span class="n">com_InitBrk</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">combuf</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">       </span>
<a id="__codelineno-242-2" name="__codelineno-242-2" href="#__codelineno-242-2"></a><span class="c1">//set up a comms ring buffer for COM0, 10 characters before overflow</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_txbufferbrk">com_TXbufferBrk</h3>
<p>This is the initialisation function for the serial communications tramsmit buffered service with the ability to sent the BREAK signal as though it is a character. The parameters are identical to <a href="#com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer()</a> except that each buffer entry can now only hold one byte. The BREAK ‘character’ is is a predefined constant call BREAK.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_TXbufferBrk(buf, buffsize, pin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the address of a buffer used for the buffering service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">bufsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the byte size of the user array provided for the buffer (each array element holds 1 byte).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">pin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the turnaround pin. If not required, just set "pin" to zero.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>

<h2 class="page-break" id="sound-control-functions">Sound Control Functions</h2>
<h3 id="snd_volume">snd_Volume</h3>
<p>Set the sound playback volume. Var must be in the range from 8 (min volume) to 127 (max volume). If var is less than 8, volume is set to 8, and if var &gt; 127 it is set to 127. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_Volume(var);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">var</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sound playback volume</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-244-1" name="__codelineno-244-1" href="#__codelineno-244-1"></a><span class="n">snd_Volume</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">127</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Set Volume to maximum </span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="snd_pitch">snd_Pitch</h3>
<p>Sets the samples playback rate to a different frequency. Setting pitch to zero restores the original sample rate. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_Pitch(pitch);</code></p>

<td style="text-align: left;">Sample's playback rate. Minimum is 4KHz. Range is, 4000 – 65535.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h3 id="snd_bufsize">snd_BufSize</h3>
<p>Specify the memory chunk size for the wavefile buffer, default size 1024 bytes. Depending on the sample size, memory constraints, and the sample quality, it may be beneficial to change the buffer size from the default size of 1024 bytes. 
This function is for control of a wav buffer, see the <a href="#file_playwav"><strong>file_PlayWAV()</strong></a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_BufSize(var);</code></p>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">var</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the buffer size. <br> 0 = 1024 bytes (default) <br> 1 = 2048 bytes <br> 2 = 4096 bytes</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>

<h3 id="snd_freq">snd_Freq</h3>
<p>Produces a pure square wave waveform. This command is designed to drive Piezo transducers which require this sort of input. It can be used directly with high impedance speakers. Whilst it also works on displays with a built-in amplifier the sound produced is extremely annoying. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_Freq(freq, duration);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">freq</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The frequency of the sound to produce, 20Hz is the minimum.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">duration</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The duration of the sound in milliseconds.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: <strong>0</strong> if note cannot be played because a frequency is playing, else returns <strong>True</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-251-1" name="__codelineno-251-1" href="#__codelineno-251-1"></a><span class="n">snd_Freq</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">2731</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// produce a 100ms burst at the Piezo’s resonant frequency. </span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="snd_rtttl">snd_RTTTL</h3>
<p>This function uses the "Ring Tone Text Transfer Language" (RTTTL) developed by Nokia for cellphone ring tones. There are certain differences that need to be taken into account, and several additions that will be described later. It is recommended to check the original format first, with the suggested reference located at: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_Tone_Transfer_Language</p>
<p>With little practice and minor modifications, most RTTTL tunes that can be downloaded off the web are playable with this function. Also, a wide range of sound effects can be made using standard RTTTL notation augmented with the additional 4DGL functions.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_RTTTL(tunePtr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">tunePtr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies a pointer to a data statement or a string constant containing RTTTL information.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The argument passed to the <strong>snd_RTTTL (...)</strong> function must be an ASCII string. If the string is passed as a pointer from a #DATA statement, it must be terminated with a zero (0x00). If a string is passed directly as a parameter, the '0' is automatically appended by the compiler as per normal strings.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Examples</em></strong></p>

<h2 class="page-break" id="spi-control-functions">SPI Control Functions</h2>
<p>The SPI functions in this section apply to any general-purpose SPI device.
To be used only when the uSD card is not active.</p>
<h3 id="spi_init">spi_Init</h3>
<p>Sets up the PIXXI-GFX2 SPI port to communicate with SPI devices.</p>
<p><img alt="SPI Mode Arguments" src="../img/pixxi/spi-mode.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Init(speed, input_mode, output_mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">speed</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the speed of the SPI port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">input_mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the input mode of the SPI port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">output_mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the output mode of the SPI port.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   None</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>The SPI functions in this section are not necessary when using the memory card or serial flash chips interfaced to the SPI port.</li>
<li>The SPI functions in this section are relevant to those devices other than the memory card and the serial flash chip used for media access. This is relevant in cases where Flash Memory or uSD card is not present, and the SPI port on PIXXI is used for another SPI device.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-253-1" name="__codelineno-253-1" href="#__codelineno-253-1"></a><span class="n">spi_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI_FAST</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">RXMODE_0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">CKMODE_0</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="spi_read">spi_Read</h3>
<p>This function allows a raw unadorned byte read from the SPI device.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Read();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Returns a single data byte from the SPI device.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-254-1" name="__codelineno-254-1" href="#__codelineno-254-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">result</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-254-2" name="__codelineno-254-2" href="#__codelineno-254-2"></a><span class="n">spi_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI_SPEED0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RXMODE_0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">CKMODE_0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-254-3" name="__codelineno-254-3" href="#__codelineno-254-3"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Hello World</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// replace with your code</span>
<a id="__codelineno-254-4" name="__codelineno-254-4" href="#__codelineno-254-4"></a><span class="c1">//...</span>
<a id="__codelineno-254-5" name="__codelineno-254-5" href="#__codelineno-254-5"></a><span class="n">spi_Write</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mh">0x40</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// x_Accel Request</span>
<a id="__codelineno-254-6" name="__codelineno-254-6" href="#__codelineno-254-6"></a><span class="nl">result</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">spi_Read</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-254-7" name="__codelineno-254-7" href="#__codelineno-254-7"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"result: "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">result</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The Chip Select line (SDCS) is lowered automatically.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="spi_write">spi_Write</h3>
<p>This function allows a raw unadorned byte write to the SPI device.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Write(byte);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Descrption</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">byte</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the data byte to be sent to the SPI device.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See the example in section <a href="#spi_read">spi_Read()</a>.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The Chip Select line (SDCS) is lowered automatically.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="spi_disable">spi_Disable</h3>
<p>This function raises the Chip Select (SDCS) line of the SPI device, disabling it from further activity. The CS line will be automatically lowered next time the SPI functions <a href="#spi_read">spi_Read()</a> or <a href="#spi_write">spi_Write(...)</a> are used, and also by action of any of the media_ functions.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Disable();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   None</p>

<h3 id="str_putbyte">str_PutByte</h3>
<p>Put a byte value into a string buffer at ptr. Similar to "POKEB" in basic.
It is not necessary for byte pointer ptr to be word aligned.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_PutByte(ptr, val);</code></p>

</tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">Byte value to insert</td>

<h3 id="str_match">str_Match</h3>
<p>Case Sensitive match.
Compares the string at position ptr in a string buffer to the string str, skipping over any leading spaces if required. If a match occurs, ptr is advanced to the first position past the match, else ptr is not altered.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Match(&amp;ptr, *str);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Descrption</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Address of byte pointer to string buffer</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer string to match</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   0 if no match, else advance ptr to the next position after the match and returns a pointer to the match position.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-264-1" name="__codelineno-264-1" href="#__codelineno-264-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">buffer</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">];</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// 200 character buffer for a source string</span>

<h3 id="str_matchi">str_MatchI</h3>
<p>Case Insensitive match.
Compares the string at position ptr in a string buffer to the string str, skipping over any leading spaces if required. If a match occurs, ptr is advanced to the first position past the match, else ptr is not altered.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_MatchI(&amp;ptr, *str);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Descrption</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Address of byte pointer to string buffer</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer string to match</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   0 if no match, else advance ptr to the next position after the match and returns a pointer to the match position.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:</p>

<h3 id="str_find">str_Find</h3>
<p>Case Sensitive.
Searches for string str in string buffer pointed to by ptr.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Find(&amp;ptr, *str);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Descrption</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Byte pointer to string buffer</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">String to find</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   0 if not found, otherwise, the position of the find if successful.</p>

<h3 id="str_printf">str_Printf</h3>
<p>This function prints a formatted string from elements derived from a structured byte region. There is only one input argument, the byte region pointer ptr which is automatically advanced as the format specifier string is processed. The format string is similar to the C language, however, there are a few differences, including the addition of the indirection token * (asterix).</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Printf(&amp;ptr, *format);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Descrption</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Byte pointer to the input data (structure).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">format</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Format string. <br><br> Format Specifiers: <br> %c - character <br> %s - string of characters <br> %d - signed decimal <br> %ld - long decimal <br> %u - unsigned decimal <br> %lu - long unsigned decimal    <br> %x - hex byte <br> %X - hex word <br> %lX - hex long <br> %b - binary word <br> %lb - long binary word <br><br> * indirection prefix (placed after '%' to specify indirect addressing) <br><br> (number) width description (use between '%' and format specifier to set the field width).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   the position of last extraction point. This is useful for processing by other string functions</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-269-1" name="__codelineno-269-1" href="#__codelineno-269-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">buffer</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">];</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// 200 character buffer for a source string</span>

<h3 id="str_cat">str_Cat</h3>
<p>Appends a copy of the source string to the destination string. The terminating null character in destination is overwritten by the first character of source, and a new null-character is appended at the end of the new string formed by the concatenation of both in destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Cat(&amp;destination, &amp;source);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Descrption</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">destination</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination string address</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">source</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Source string address</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   pointer to the destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-270-1" name="__codelineno-270-1" href="#__codelineno-270-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">buf</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">];</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// 200 character buffer for a source string</span>

<a id="__codelineno-270-4" name="__codelineno-270-4" href="#__codelineno-270-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">p</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>

<a id="__codelineno-270-8" name="__codelineno-270-8" href="#__codelineno-270-8"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">str_Cat</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">p</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">"There"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Will append "There" to the end of buf</span>

<a id="__codelineno-270-10" name="__codelineno-270-10" href="#__codelineno-270-10"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">repeat</span>

<h3 id="str_catn">str_CatN</h3>
<p>The number of characters copied is limited by "<strong>count</strong>".
The terminating null character in destination is overwritten by the first character of source, and a new null-character is appended at the end of the new string formed by the concatenation of both in destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_CatN(&amp;ptr, str, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Descrption</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination string address</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Source string address</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of characters to be concatenated</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   pointer to the destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-271-1" name="__codelineno-271-1" href="#__codelineno-271-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">buf</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">];</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// 200 character buffer for a source string</span>
<a id="__codelineno-271-2" name="__codelineno-271-2" href="#__codelineno-271-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-271-3" name="__codelineno-271-3" href="#__codelineno-271-3"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>
<a id="__codelineno-271-4" name="__codelineno-271-4" href="#__codelineno-271-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">p</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-271-5" name="__codelineno-271-5" href="#__codelineno-271-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">buf</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>

<a id="__codelineno-271-8" name="__codelineno-271-8" href="#__codelineno-271-8"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">str_CatN</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">p</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">"Monday"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Concatenate "Mon" to the end of buf</span>

<h3 id="str_bytemove">str_ByteMove</h3>
<p>Copy bytes from "<strong>src</strong>" to "<strong>dest</strong>", stopping only when "<strong>count</strong>" is exhausted. No terminator is appended, it is purely a byte copy, and any zeroes encountered will also be copied.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_ByteMove(src, dest, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Descrption</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">src</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned source</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned destination</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of bytes to transfer</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   a pointer to the end of the destination (which is "<strong>dest</strong>" + "<strong>count</strong>").</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-272-1" name="__codelineno-272-1" href="#__codelineno-272-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">src</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">dest</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mybuf1</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mybuf2</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">];</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// string pointers and two 20 byte buffers</span>
<a id="__codelineno-272-2" name="__codelineno-272-2" href="#__codelineno-272-2"></a><span class="n">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf1</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"TESTING 123"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-272-3" name="__codelineno-272-3" href="#__codelineno-272-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-272-4" name="__codelineno-272-4" href="#__codelineno-272-4"></a><span class="nl">src</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">strPtr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf1</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-272-5" name="__codelineno-272-5" href="#__codelineno-272-5"></a><span class="nl">dest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str_Ptr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf2</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-272-6" name="__codelineno-272-6" href="#__codelineno-272-6"></a><span class="n">src</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">+=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// move src pointer to "G 123"</span>

<a id="__codelineno-272-8" name="__codelineno-272-8" href="#__codelineno-272-8"></a><span class="n">str_ByteMove</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">src</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">dest</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="c1">// move to second buffer (including the zero terminator)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-272-9" name="__codelineno-272-9" href="#__codelineno-272-9"></a>

<a id="__codelineno-272-11" name="__codelineno-272-11" href="#__codelineno-272-11"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-272-12" name="__codelineno-272-12" href="#__codelineno-272-12"></a><span class="nl">nextpos</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str_ByteMove</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">d</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="str_copy">str_Copy</h3>
<p>Copy a string from "<strong>src</strong>" to "<strong>dest</strong>", stopping only when the end of source string "<strong>src</strong>" is encountered (0x00 terminator). The terminator is always appended, even if "<strong>src</strong>" is an empty string.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Copy(dest, src);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Descrption</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned destination</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">src</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned source</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   a pointer to the 0x00 string terminator at the end of "<strong>dest</strong>" (which is "<strong>dest</strong>" + <a href="#str_length">str_Length(src);</a>).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-273-1" name="__codelineno-273-1" href="#__codelineno-273-1"></a><span class="nl">nextplace</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str_Copy</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">d</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="str_copyn">str_CopyN</h3>
<p>Copy a string from "<strong>src</strong>" to "<strong>dest</strong>", stopping only when "<strong>count</strong>" is exhausted, or end of source string "<strong>src</strong>" is encountered (0x00 string terminator). The terminator is always appended, even if "<strong>count</strong>" is zero, or "<strong>src</strong>" is a null string.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_CopyN(dest, src, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Descrption</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned destination</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">src</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned source</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Maximum number of bytes to copy</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   a pointer to the 0x00 string terminator at the end of "<strong>dest</strong>" (which is "<strong>dest</strong>" + <a href="#str_length">str_Length(src);</a>).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-274-1" name="__codelineno-274-1" href="#__codelineno-274-1"></a><span class="nl">nextplace</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str_CopyN</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">d</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h2 class="page-break" id="text-and-string-functions">Text and String Functions</h2>
<h3 id="txt_movecursor">txt_MoveCursor</h3>
<p>Moves the text cursor to a screen position set by line and column parameters. The line and column position is calculated, based on the size and scaling factor for the currently selected font. When text is outputted to screen it will be displayed from this position. The text position could also be set with <a href="#gfx_moveto">gfx_MoveTo(...)</a>; if required to set the text position to an exact pixel location. Note that lines and columns start from 0. So, line 0, column 0 is the top left corner of the display.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>txt_MoveCursor(line, column);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">line</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Holds a positive value for the required line position.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">column</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Holds a positive value for the required column position.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-277-1" name="__codelineno-277-1" href="#__codelineno-277-1"></a><span class="n">txt_MoveCursor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">4</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">9</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-277-2" name="__codelineno-277-2" href="#__codelineno-277-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-277-3" name="__codelineno-277-3" href="#__codelineno-277-3"></a><span class="c1">// This example moves the text origin to the 5th line and the 10th column.</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="putstr">putstr</h3>
<p>This function prints a string to the current output stream, usually the display. The argument can be a string constant, a pointer to a string, a pointer to an array, or a pointer to a data statement.</p>
<p>The output of <strong>putstr</strong> can be redirected to the communications port, the media, or memory using the <a href="#to">to(...)</a> function.</p>
<p>A string constant is automatically terminated with a zero. A string in a data statement is not automatically terminated with a zero.</p>
<p>All variables in 4DGL are 16-bit, if an array is used for holding 8-bit characters, each array element packs 1 or 2 characters. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>putstr(ponter);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pointer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A string constant or pointer to a string.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The pointer to the item that was printed.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="putnum">putnum</h3>
<p><strong>putnum</strong> prints a 16bit number in various formats to the current output stream, usually the display.</p>
<p id="number_formatting"> Number formatting bits supplied by format</p>

<p><img alt="numberFormating" src="../img/pixxi/numberformatting1.png"></p>
<p id="format_constant">Pre-Defined format constant quick reference</p>

<div class="tabbed-set tabbed-alternate" data-tabs="8:4" style="--md-indicator-x: 16px; --md-indicator-width: 84px;"><input checked="checked" id="__tabbed_8_1" name="__tabbed_8" type="radio"><input id="__tabbed_8_2" name="__tabbed_8" type="radio"><input id="__tabbed_8_3" name="__tabbed_8" type="radio"><input id="__tabbed_8_4" name="__tabbed_8" type="radio"><div class="tabbed-labels"><label for="__tabbed_8_1">DECIMAL</label><label for="__tabbed_8_2">UNSIGNED DECIMAL</label><label for="__tabbed_8_3">HEX</label><label for="__tabbed_8_4">BINARY</label></div>
<div class="tabbed-content">
<div class="tabbed-block">
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">DEC</td>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>putnum(format, value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">format</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A constant that specifies the number format.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The number to be printed.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The default width of the numeric field (digit count), usually ignored.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-283-1" name="__codelineno-283-1" href="#__codelineno-283-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">v</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-283-2" name="__codelineno-283-2" href="#__codelineno-283-2"></a><span class="nl">v</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mo">0567</span><span class="mi">8</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-283-3" name="__codelineno-283-3" href="#__codelineno-283-3"></a><span class="n">putnum</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">HEX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">v</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">             </span><span class="c1">// print the number as hex 4 digits</span>
<a id="__codelineno-283-4" name="__codelineno-283-4" href="#__codelineno-283-4"></a><span class="n">putnum</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BIN</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">v</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">             </span><span class="c1">//print the number as binary 16 digits</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="print">print</h3>
<p><strong>4DGL</strong> has a versatile <a href="#print">print(...)</a> statement for formatting numbers and strings. In it's simplest form, print will simply print a number as can be seen below:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-284-1" name="__codelineno-284-1" href="#__codelineno-284-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-284-2" name="__codelineno-284-2" href="#__codelineno-284-2"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-284-3" name="__codelineno-284-3" href="#__codelineno-284-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-284-4" name="__codelineno-284-4" href="#__codelineno-284-4"></a><span class="c1">// This will print **100** to the current output device (usually the display in TEXT mode). </span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>If you wish to add a string anywhere within a <a href="#print">print(...)</a> statement, just place a quoted string expression and you will be able to mix strings and numbers in a variety of formats. See the following example.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-285-1" name="__codelineno-285-1" href="#__codelineno-285-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"the value of myvar is :- "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"and its 8bit binary representation is:-"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">BIN8</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
</div>
<p>(*) Refer the table in <a href="#putnum">putnum(..)</a> for all the numeric representations available.</p>
<p>The <a href="#print">print(...)</a> statement will accept directives passed in square brackets to make it print in various ways, for instance, if you wish to print a number in 4 digit hex, use the <strong>[HEX4]</strong> directive placed in front of the variable to be displayed within the print statement. See the following example.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-286-1" name="__codelineno-286-1" href="#__codelineno-286-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"myvar as a 4 digit HEX number is :- "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">HEX4</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>There are 2 print directives that are not part of the numeric set and will be explained separately. these are the <strong>[STR]</strong> and <strong>[CHR]</strong> directives.</p>
</div>
<p>The <strong>[STR]</strong> directive expects a string pointer to follow:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-287-1" name="__codelineno-287-1" href="#__codelineno-287-1"></a><span class="nl">s</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"Hello World"</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// assign a string constant to s </span>
<a id="__codelineno-287-2" name="__codelineno-287-2" href="#__codelineno-287-2"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Var 's' points to a string constant at address"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">s</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">" which is"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">STR</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>The <strong>[CHR]</strong> directive prints the character value of a variable.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-288-1" name="__codelineno-288-1" href="#__codelineno-288-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"The third character of the string is '"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">CHR</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">s</span><span class="o">+</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">));</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>also</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-289-1" name="__codelineno-289-1" href="#__codelineno-289-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"The value of 'myvar' as an ASCII charater is '"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">CHR</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>You can freely mix string pointers, strings, variables and expressions within a print statement. <a href="#print">print(...)</a> can also use the <a href="#to">to(...)</a> function to redirect it's output to a different output device other than the screen using the function (refer to the <a href="#to">to(...)</a> statement for further examples).</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>print(...);</code>    </p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-290-1" name="__codelineno-290-1" href="#__codelineno-290-1"></a><span class="c1">/////////////////////</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-2" name="__codelineno-290-2" href="#__codelineno-290-2"></a><span class="c1">// DATA STATEMENT  //</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-3" name="__codelineno-290-3" href="#__codelineno-290-3"></a><span class="c1">/////////////////////</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-4" name="__codelineno-290-4" href="#__codelineno-290-4"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-290-5" name="__codelineno-290-5" href="#__codelineno-290-5"></a><span class="cp">#DATA</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-6" name="__codelineno-290-6" href="#__codelineno-290-6"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">word</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myData</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-7" name="__codelineno-290-7" href="#__codelineno-290-7"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">myString1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Bert</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Fred</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">main</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myString2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">baud</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">barney</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x1111</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mh">0x2222</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mh">0x3333</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mh">0x4444</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-8" name="__codelineno-290-8" href="#__codelineno-290-8"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-290-9" name="__codelineno-290-9" href="#__codelineno-290-9"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">byte</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myString1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"Data String OK</span><span class="se">\n\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">0</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-10" name="__codelineno-290-10" href="#__codelineno-290-10"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">byte</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myString2</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\"</span><span class="s">(and forward referenced!)</span><span class="se">\"\n\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">0</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-11" name="__codelineno-290-11" href="#__codelineno-290-11"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">word</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">baud</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">150</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">300</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">600</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">1200</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">2400</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">9600</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-12" name="__codelineno-290-12" href="#__codelineno-290-12"></a><span class="cp">#END</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-13" name="__codelineno-290-13" href="#__codelineno-290-13"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-290-14" name="__codelineno-290-14" href="#__codelineno-290-14"></a><span class="c1">// this constant is a forward reference</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-15" name="__codelineno-290-15" href="#__codelineno-290-15"></a><span class="cp">#constant barney 9876</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-16" name="__codelineno-290-16" href="#__codelineno-290-16"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-290-17" name="__codelineno-290-17" href="#__codelineno-290-17"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Fred</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str</span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-18" name="__codelineno-290-18" href="#__codelineno-290-18"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"string = "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">STR</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-19" name="__codelineno-290-19" href="#__codelineno-290-19"></a><span class="n">endfunc</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-20" name="__codelineno-290-20" href="#__codelineno-290-20"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-290-21" name="__codelineno-290-21" href="#__codelineno-290-21"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Bert</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">p1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">p2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">p3</span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-22" name="__codelineno-290-22" href="#__codelineno-290-22"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"hello from Bert</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">p1="</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">p1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">p2="</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">p2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">p3="</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">p3</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-23" name="__codelineno-290-23" href="#__codelineno-290-23"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="k">return</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"Bert was here</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-24" name="__codelineno-290-24" href="#__codelineno-290-24"></a><span class="n">endfunc</span>
<a id="__codelineno-290-25" name="__codelineno-290-25" href="#__codelineno-290-25"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-290-26" name="__codelineno-290-26" href="#__codelineno-290-26"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">main</span><span class="p">()</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="to">to</h3>
<p><a href="#to">to()</a> sends the printed output to destinations other than the screen. Normally, print just sends its output to the display in <strong>TEXT</strong> mode which is the default, however, the output from print can be sent to 'streams', e.g. – <strong>COM0</strong>, <strong>COM1</strong>, an open FAT16 file with <strong>DSK</strong>, to raw media with <strong>MDA</strong> (media), or to the I2C ports with <strong>I2C</strong>.</p>
<p>The <strong>to(...)</strong> function can also stream to a memory array . Note that once the function has taken effect, the stream reverts back to the default stream which is <strong>TEXT</strong> as soon as <a href="#putch">putch</a>, <a href="#putstr">putstr</a>, <a href="#putnum">putnum</a>, <a href="#print">print</a>, or <a href="#str_printf">str_Printf</a> has completed its action.</p>
<p>The <strong>APPEND</strong> argument is used to append the printed output to the same place as the previous redirection. This is most useful for building string arrays, or adding sequential data to a media stream.</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Predefined Name</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Constant</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">putch, putstr, putnum, print, str_Printf redirection destination</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">DSK</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF802</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the most recently open file that has been opened in write mode.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">COM0</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xFF04</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is redirected to the <strong>COM0</strong> (default serial) port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">COM1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xFF08</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is redirected to the <strong>COM1</strong> port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF820</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the <strong>I2C</strong> port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">MDA</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xFF40</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the <strong>SD/SDHC</strong> or <strong>FLASH</strong> media.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">APPEND</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0x0000</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is appended to user array if previous redirection was to an array.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">(memory pointer)</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Array Address</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is redirect to the <strong>memory</strong> pointer argument.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<div class="admonition warning">
<p class="admonition-title">Warning</p>
<p>Becareful writing to a FAT16 formatted card without checking legal partitioned are, else the disk formatting will be destroyed.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>to(outstream);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">outstream</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A variable or constant specifying the destination for the <a href="#putch">putch</a>, <a href="#putstr">putstr</a>, <a href="#putnum">putnum</a>, <a href="#print">print</a> and <a href="#str_printf">str_Printf</a> functions.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="charwidth">charwidth</h3>
<p><strong>charwidth</strong> is used to calculate the width in pixel units for a character, based on the currently selected font.
The font can be proportional or mono spaced. If the total width of the string exceeds 255 pixel units, the function will return the 'wrapped' (modulo 8) value.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>charwidth('char');</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The ascii character for the width calculation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The width of a single character in pixel units.</p>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="charheight">charheight</h3>
<p><strong>charheight</strong> is used to calculate the height in pixel units for a character, based on the currently selected font.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>charheight('char');</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The ascii character for the height calculation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The height of a single character in pixel units.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth</a>.</p>
<h3 id="strwidth">strwidth</h3>
<p><strong>strwidth</strong> returns the width of a zero terminated string in pixel units. Note that any string constants declared in your program are automatically terminated with a zero as an end marker by the compiler. Any string that you create in the DATA section or MEM section must have a zero added as a terminator for this function to work correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>strwidth(pointer);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pointer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The pointer to a zero (0x00) terminated string.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The width of a string in pixel units, can be multi line.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth</a>.</p>
<h3 class="page-break" id="strheight">strheight</h3>
<p><strong>strheight</strong> returns the height of a zero terminated string in pixel units. The <a href="#strwidth">strwidth</a> function must be called first which makes available width and height. Note that any string constants declared in your program are automatically terminated with a zero as an end marker by the compiler. Any string that you create in the DATA section or MEM section must have a zero added as a terminator for this function to work correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>strheight();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The height of a string in pixel units, can be multi line.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth</a>.</p>
<h3 id="strlen">strlen</h3>
<p><strong>strlen</strong> returns the length of a zero terminated string in character units. Note that any string constants declared in your program are automatically terminated with a zero as an end marker by the compiler. Any string that you create in the DATA section or MEM section must have a zero added as a terminator for this function to work correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>strlen(pointer);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pointer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The pointer to a zero (0x00) terminated string.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The length of a string in character units.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth</a>.</p>
<h3 class="page-break" id="txt_set">txt_Set</h3>
<p>Given a function number and a value, set the required text control parameter, such as size, colour, and other formatting controls. This function is extremely useful in a loop to select multiple parameters from a data statement or a control array. Note also that each function available for <a href="#txt_set">txt_Set</a> has a <a href="#single_parameter_shortcuts">single parameter 'shortcut' function</a> that has the same effect.</p>
